Our customers are some of the most demanding enterprise legal departments in the world, and they hold us to a high bar on security, privacy, and responsible AI.

We're looking for a senior leader to take ownership of security and compliance as we scale.

The Role

GRC Leads own security and compliance at Wordsmith end-to-end — setting the strategy for IT and infrastructure security, running our certification program across SOC 2, ISO 27001, and ISO 42001, embedding responsible-AI practices into how we build and ship product, and making sure privacy and regulatory obligations (GDPR and beyond) are handled properly as we grow.

This is a senior role that blends strategy and hands-on execution. You'll set multi-year direction, represent Wordsmith's security posture to executives, customers, and — as we grow — the board, and build the team, tooling, and controls the company needs at the next stage, not just maintain what exists today.

What You'll Do

Security Strategy & Leadership

  • Own Wordsmith's multi-year IT security and compliance roadmap — setting priorities, budget, and tooling decisions in partnership with Engineering and company leadership.

IT & Infrastructure Security

  • Own security architecture across corporate IT and infrastructure — identity & access management, endpoint protection, and cloud/network security — and lead incident response when issues arise.

Compliance & Certification

  • Own SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001/27017/27018, and ISO 42001 end-to-end — policies, controls, audit evidence, and the audits themselves.

AI Governance

  • Run our AI governance program, including AI Impact Assessments and model/AI-vendor risk reviews, ensuring responsible, compliant AI use across the product.

Privacy Operations

  • Own privacy operations end-to-end — GDPR and other regulatory obligations, DPIAs, RoPA maintenance, sub-processor management, and Data Subject Request fulfilment.

Third-Party & Vendor Risk

  • Assess vendors and AI tools for security, privacy, and AI risk before they're adopted, and put the right contractual safeguards in place at a program level.

Team & Function Building

  • Build the people, process, and tooling the function needs as it scales — starting as the senior owner of the program today, with a mandate to build out a team as Wordsmith grows.

Executive & Board Reporting

  • Own risk and compliance reporting to leadership and, as we scale, the board — translating technical risk into business terms.

Customer & Deal Support

  • Act as the senior voice on security for enterprise deals — security questionnaires, DPAs, and our Trust Center — partnering with Sales, Customer Success, and Legal to unblock deals without cutting corners.

Automation & Tooling

  • Build lean, automation-first tooling (e.g. Vanta) for evidence collection and ongoing compliance monitoring, so the program scales without scaling headcount unnecessarily.

What we're looking for

Essential

  • 8-10+ years in security, IT, or compliance roles, including a track record of owning a security or compliance function end-to-end at a fast-growing SaaS or tech company.

  • Proven experience building or scaling a security/compliance program from an early stage — ideally including time as the sole or founding owner of the function.

  • Deep, hands-on expertise across SOC 2, the ISO 27000 series, and ideally ISO 42001.

  • Strong grounding in core IT security fundamentals — identity & access management, endpoint/device security, and cloud or network infrastructure security.

  • Practical, working knowledge of GDPR and related privacy regulation (ePrivacy or similar).

  • Experience presenting security posture, risk, and roadmap to executives, boards, or investors.

  • Experience building and/or managing a team — or a clear point of view on how you'd grow one as the function scales.

  • Comfortable owning budget and vendor decisions at a strategic level, not just executing against someone else's plan.

  • A strong cross-functional operator and executive communicator, bridging Security, IT, Legal/Privacy, Engineering, and GTM.

Valued

  • Prior experience as a Head of Security, Director of Security/IT, or similar senior/leadership title.

  • Relevant certifications — e.g. CISSP/ISC2, CISM, AIGP, CIPP/E, CIPT, CCSK, or FIP.

  • Experience in legal tech, AI, or another highly regulated SaaS environment.

  • Experience designing AI risk or impact-assessment processes from scratch.

  • Familiarity with tools such as Datagrail, MineOS, Whistic, or SafeBase.

Why this role matters

You'll take a senior leadership seat over security and compliance, with real ownership over how the function is shaped and grown.

You'll sit at the centre of trust for a fast-growing legal AI platform, directly enabling enterprise sales and customer confidence.

You'll have a clear path to building and leading a team as the function scales with the company.

What you can expect

A small, focused leadership group where your work has visible, immediate impact.

Competitive compensation, benefits, and meaningful equity.

How we work

We're an in-office team in Edinburgh. We work together because it helps us collaborate closely across product, engineering, and legal teams. You should expect to be in the office as your default.

This is a high ownership role. You'll be trusted to set strategy, represent security to executives and customers, and drive outcomes without heavy oversight.

Partner across teams - Work symbiotically with the Customer Success Manager who owns retention of your portfolio: they keep accounts healthy and renewing, you drive growth on renewal, cross-sell and expansion. Partner with Sales on handover and with Product on what customers need next.

Be the voice of the customer - Feed what you hear back to the product and commercial teams so we build and sell the right things.

In your first 12 months: you have beaten your growth quota, landed at least one major cross-sell that opened a new part of a customer's business, and your forecast is one the leadership team relies on.

Experience - At least 3 years of enterprise selling, with a consistent record of beating quota and growing enterprise accounts repeatedly and across multiple accounts. You are comfortable selling to the C-suite and General Counsel, and you have led complex, multi-stakeholder deals through procurement and security review.

Commercially Minded - You understand how to grow an account, you are comfortable talking price and value, and you connect daily customer work to retention and expansion outcomes.

Strong bias for action - You create opportunities rather than wait for them. When you see a gap in an account, you have a plan to close it by the end of the week.

A clear communicator - Comfortable writing and speaking with customers daily, and you can make technical things feel simple.

An exceptional operator - You run a disciplined pipeline, call your number accurately, and never let a follow-up slip, however busy the quarter gets.

  • A team that ships fast, cares about customers, and will invest in your growth.

arbeitnow:group-data-protection-officer-.description:
Group Data Protection Officer | M-KOPA

Remote (covering Kenya, Uganda, Nigeria, Ghana, South Africa and the UK)

You're the lawyer people call when a data question has no easy answer. You're accomplished. You're respected. You're probably even happy. But is your work protecting millions of people who are trusting a formal financial service with their personal information for the very first time?

That is the question at the heart of this role.

The trust you'd be protecting

M-KOPA now serves 10 million customers, up from 5 million in 2024, and has unlocked $2+ billion in credit. 86% of our customers report an improved quality of life, 70% use our products to earn an income, and 55% are accessing products and services for the first time. Behind them stand 2,300+ employees and 35,000 agents. Every one of those customers has handed us personal information, and they did it because they believed we would handle it with care. Across Ghana, Nigeria, Kenya, South Africa, Uganda and the UK, that belief is held under six different sets of rules, each with its own expectations about consent, retention, cross-border transfers and what happens when something goes wrong. The customers who benefit most from what we build are often the ones with the least room to absorb a mistake with their data, and that is the standard this role exists to hold.

Why this timing matters

You may have seen us advertising several roles across Legal, Risk and Compliance. That is deliberate, not random. We've moved from 5 million customers to 7 million, and we are now building beyond 10 million. The legal, risk and privacy foundations have to be laid ahead of that growth, not scrambled together after it. New markets, new products and new partners all arrive with new data questions. Joining now means shaping the privacy programme while its biggest chapters are still ahead of it.

What makes this different

In many organisations, the data protection officer reviews things at the end of the process. Here, the role reaches the whole group. Your current role: one jurisdiction, one regime. This role: six markets, one customer promise.

You would report day to day to the Chief Legal, Risk and Compliance Officer, with reporting to the CEO and the Board as well. Your recommendations on strategy and implementation go to the people who run the company, and they shape how the business executes. Your work also connects directly to our mission. Financial inclusion only works if the people we serve can trust us with what they share, and you would be one of the people who keeps that trust earned. Because the role spans the whole group, you would also see patterns that no single market team can: where the same gap appears in several places, and where one fix can protect every customer at once.

What you'll bring

  • Qualified lawyer with extensive, progressive experience in data protection and privacy compliance, including running privacy operations end to end: data protection impact assessments, transfer impact assessments, vendor assessments and risk management.

  • Detailed command of data protection law across our six markets, paired with a sound understanding of information systems, data processing operations and security needs, so you can challenge the architecture as confidently as the contract.

  • Demonstrable experience developing policies, guidelines and template clauses for the processing of personal data, and proficiency in using AI tools responsibly to support privacy research, compliance work and risk assessment.

A recognised privacy or security certification (CIPP, CIPT, or ISO 27001 or 27701 implementer or auditor) is an added advantage. It is not a gate.

What you'll actually do

  • Run the programme and fix what you find. Lead remediation and data audits, conduct DPIAs, identify where we are partially or fully non-compliant, and put it right across all six markets, while keeping the records of processing that prove it.

  • Build the tools everyone else uses. Write the guidelines, template clauses and contracts that govern how partners, suppliers and vendors handle personal information, and support the privacy software, incident response and breach notification procedures behind them.

  • Turn the law into culture. Design training and internal communications for staff, run awareness for third parties, and support due diligence, certification, audits and new-market expansion, so data protection is something every team does rather than something Legal does to them.

The reality check

This role is demanding. You will hold six regimes in your head at once, advise colleagues who would rather hear a different answer, and move a business forward with clear, plain-English advice. It is an onsite role, and your calendar will hold the strategic and the urgent in the same week: a policy redesign on Monday, a vendor assessment on Wednesday, a breach notification drill on Friday. The work rewards people who like building systems that still work when nobody is watching. You're probably ready for exactly this.

Ready to build the privacy standard 10 million customers can rely on?

If you read the question at the top of this page and felt something, that is probably the signal. Let's talk.

Why M-KOPA?

At M-KOPA, we empower our people to own their careers through diverse development programs, coaching partnerships, and on-the-job training. We support individual journeys with family-friendly policies, prioritize well-being, and embrace flexibility.

Join us in shaping the future of M-KOPA as we grow together. Explore more at m-kopa.com.

Recognized four times by the Financial Times as one Africa's fastest growing companies (2022, 2023, 2024, 2025 and 2026), named on CNBC's World’s Top Fintech Companies 2025 & 2026 and by TIME100 Most influential companies in the world 2023 and 2024 , we've served over 10 million customers, unlocking $2 billion in cumulative credit for the everyday earners across Africa, in addition to over 10,000 e-bikes financed in Kenya.

arbeitnow:head-of-security-london-85077.description:
LOCATION: London, UK preferred. US & EU candidates will be considered. then US, then EU.

Option A: £400-500/day ~2.5 days/week, contract.
Option B: £120,000 base, full-time.

We are open to two profiles:

  • Head of Security (part-time contract, ~2.5 days/week): an information security lead covering the full scope below.

  • Head of Security & Security Engineer (full-time): the same scope, plus hands-on technical security engineering. This is highlighted in the additional engineering scope below.

Please tell us in your application which you are applying for and what your availability and notice period are.

About

The AI Whistleblower Initiative (https://aiwi.org) is an independent non-profit supporting frontier AI insiders who want to raise concerns. We do this through outreach and education of insiders, access to vetted legal and financial resources, and policy work. Our insights help strengthen internal and government reporting channels, advocate for better legislation, and promote the conditions under which concerns can reach the people best placed to act on them, with source protection at their core. Find a selection of our work here (https://aiwi.org/our-work).

Most high-stakes moments in AI over the coming years will involve frontier company insiders having and raising concerns: within companies, to regulators, or through other pathways.

Those insiders tell us they face enormous uncertainty along the “concern raising” path -- from detecting concerns to whether and how to voice concerns with maximum impact and minimal risk, which even legally protected whistleblowing can carry. To date, no organization has dedicated itself deeply to delivering the best strategic, frontier-AI-specific guidance to these individuals, their supporters, and their attorneys (our partners). We exist to ensure that each insider disclosure is maximally impactful and safe for the person making the disclosure.

Tasks

About the role

The Head of Security is a dual inward- and outward-facing role. You will update, design and implement AIWI’s internal security posture, and provide external guidance to AI insiders, whistleblowers and partners. You will create and oversee internal security controls, manage an evolving risk appetite, and design internal policies and trainings so that staff stay safe and secure in their everyday workflows. You will also design and deliver training and guidance to would-be whistleblowers and AIWI’s partners.

In other words, you are as comfortable drafting an internal security policy or building an onboarding and device-provisioning plan as you are training whistleblowers on how to evade insider-threat-management (ITM) systems, or explaining natural language watermarking. You can design, implement, and enforce a coherent data governance policy, and you understand the intricacies of watermarking schemes and counter-forensic measures against them.

You will report to Karl Koch, our CEO, and work closely with our co-founder/technical advisor Max and the principal engineer we are hiring. You will manage potential contractors and propose spend, with CEO sign-off on budget. Our environment is highly sensitive: so confidentiality, careful judgement, and conviction in what we do are essential.

Areas of Ownership

1. Internal security and compliance.

  • Onboarding, access rights, information sharing

  • Working with trustworthy contractors

  • Tooling: audit of all tool configurations, and keeping critical software (e.g., our GlobaLeaks instance) up to date

  • Incident policy and response

  • Security input and strategy on new technology and developments

  • Full review of the current setup, identifying vulnerabilities to inform wider strategy and next steps

  • IT helpdesking (supporting Operations to field the right ones your way)

2. External: insiders and coalition members.

  • Guidance, video content, and op-eds

  • Assisting coalition members

  • Device provisioning

  • Being “ready” to urgently support security needs

  • Further services/offerings

3. Security engineering (full-time track only).

  • You will build and run the technical security layer behind AIWI’s internal and external systems, working alongside the Principal Engineer (e.g. Harden and monitor our self-hosted, set up; Build security tooling, automation, and detections in-house; Review architecture and code, and secure CI/CD and the software supply chain; Run offensive testing (pen tests, red teaming) on our own systems and tools, including our GlobaLeaks instance; Lead technical incident response and forensics; Take security engineering work off the Principal Engineer so they can focus on product delivery)

Requirements

Core (both profiles)

  • Experience working with and securing journalists, sources, whistleblowers, or others in high-risk sensitive environments.

  • Proven track record of delivering security trainings to diverse audiences in a variety of environments.

  • Demonstrated experience in source protection (how have you helped journalists or non-profits safeguard sources?).

  • Deep knowledge of secure platforms (e.g., able to explain the security differences between Signal and SimpleX, or between Qubes and Tails).

  • Proficiency in operational security, threat modeling, and risk management.

  • Familiarity with IDS, ITM, and DLP suites, and how to safeguard whistleblowers against these systems.

  • Experience drafting, enacting, and enforcing internal security controls and policies.

  • Knowledge of document, audio, and video watermarking systems, and counter-forensics.

  • Genuine, demonstrable commitment to AI safety and whistleblower protection.

  • 5-15 years experience, dependent on the projects you have worked on.

Additional for the full-time profile

  • Hands-on experience as a security engineer or builder, with a track record of shipping security tooling and infrastructure.

  • Strong coding skills in one or more of Python, Go, Rust, or C/C++, plus shell. You write security tooling, automation, and detections yourself, without relying on AI tools.

arbeitnow:senior-software-engineer-genai.description:
Our Global Structure


Deliveroo is now part of DoorDash, bringing together teams with even greater reach, scale, and ambition. Depending on your role, you may collaborate with teammates, systems, and leaders across DoorDash and Wolt. Together, we're unlocking new possibilities as one global team.

Senior Software Engineer, GenAI Platform

 

About the Team

Deliveroo's GenAI Platform team sits within Machine Learning Platform and builds the shared infrastructure that helps DoorDash, Wolt, and Deliveroo teams safely bring GenAI-powered products, agents, automation, and personalisation to production. Our mission is to increase the velocity of business impact from GenAI. A central pillar of that work is running frontier open-weight LLMs and VLMs (such as GLM, Qwen, Kimi, and DeepSeek) ourselves — real-time GPU serving, high-throughput batch inference, and fine-tuning on autoscaling GPUs — delivering large cost and latency wins (for example, a billion embeddings produced roughly 20× cheaper and visual models served roughly 72% cheaper). We also own core platform surfaces including the LLM Gateway, Agent Gateway, evals infrastructure, guardrails, and cost attribution.

 

About the Role

You will join a small, high-leverage team building production infrastructure for Generative AI at Deliveroo and DoorDash, leading the design and architecture of our open-weights model platform spanning inference and fine-tuning: real-time GPU serving, high-throughput batch inference, and model fine-tuning. You'll set technical direction across model serving and inference engines, fine-tuning and training pipelines, GPU autoscaling and utilization, batch pipelines, backend services, and observability, and mentor engineers as you go. This role is ideal for a senior engineer who enjoys owning ambiguous, high-impact systems and pushing the cost/performance frontier of GPU inference and fine-tuning in a fast-moving technical area where product needs, model capabilities, vendor ecosystems, and cost/performance tradeoffs are evolving quickly.

 

You're excited about this opportunity because you will…

  • Lead the design of infrastructure that helps teams move GenAI ideas from prototype to production, increasing the velocity of business impact from AI across the company.

  • Own and evolve our open-weights serving stack — real-time GPU endpoints, high-throughput batch inference, and fine-tuning (SFT/DPO/LoRA) — alongside the LLM Gateway, Agent Gateway, evals infrastructure, guardrails, and cost attribution.

  • Architect scalable, high-performance systems for model serving, batch inference, GPU autoscaling, and fine-tuning that power real customer and internal automation use cases

  • Push the cost and latency frontier of GPU inference — turning batch jobs that took days into hours and cutting inference cost by multiples — while giving product teams a clean choice across open-weight and closed-source models with reliability, fallback, observability, and cost controls built in.

  • Build platforms that support rapid experimentation while meeting production standards for latency, scale, monitoring, SLOs, playbooks, and operational excellence.

  • Partner closely with — and raise the technical bar for — ML engineers, product engineers, data scientists, and platform teams across DoorDash, Wolt, and Deliveroo to turn emerging GenAI capabilities into durable platform primitives.

  • Set technical direction for the future of the company's centralised GenAI platform — including emerging directions such as reinforcement learning (RLHF/RLVR), agent optimisation, and other post-training and agentic techniques — enabling the next generation of AI-powered products, agents, automation, and personalisation.

 

We're excited about you because…

  • BSc, MSc or PhD in Computer Science or equivalent

  • 5+ years of industry experience in software engineering

  • Deep backend engineering fundamentals, especially in Python and distributed systems.

  • Track record of designing and owning production services, APIs, data pipelines, or ML infrastructure at scale.

  • Experience operating systems in production, including observability, debugging, reliability, incident response, and performance/cost optimization.

  • Deep hands-on experience with LLM inference and/or fine-tuning of open-weight models in production — serving (latency, throughput, batching, autoscaling, GPU utilization) and/or fine-tuning (SFT/DPO/LoRA).

  • Demonstrated technical leadership: leading design across ambiguous, fast-moving technical areas, mentoring engineers, and turning customer use cases into reusable platform capabilities

  • Proficiency in using AI coding tools (e.g., Claude Code, Codex, Cursor) in the full software development lifecycle, including designing, generating code, testing, monitoring and releasing software

 

Nice To Haves

  • Experience with LLM inference engines and serving frameworks (e.g., vLLM, SGLang, TensorRT-LLM) in production

  • Experience with distributed/multi-node fine-tuning and training pipelines (SFT, DPO/RLHF, LoRA), including data preparation and evaluation

  • GPU performance work — multi-node/distributed inference, KV-cache/memory optimisation, quantisation (FP8/INT8/AWQ/GPTQ), or cold-start/throughput tuning

  • Experience with Kubernetes, cloud infrastructure (AWS/GCP), GPUs, serverless/elastic GPU platforms (e.g., Modal), or high-throughput batch systems

  • Experience with LLM gateways, model routing, vendor abstraction, or cost attribution

  • Experience building developer platforms, internal platforms, or self-serve infrastructure

  • Experience building and deploying AI agents or MCP servers in production

  • Experience with eval systems, LLM observability, tracing, RAG, search, or vector databases

Diversity, Equity and Inclusion

At Deliveroo, we know that a great workplace reflects the world around us and that true diversity and inclusion make us stronger, more creative, and better at what we do. We're committed to fostering an environment where everyone can do their best work and feel they belong.

We believe in equality of opportunity and welcome candidates from all backgrounds regardless of age, gender, ethnicity, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity, socio-economic background, religion, or belief.

We'll share details on how to request support so we can ensure you have a fair and equitable experience.

If you're excited about making a real impact in a fast-moving marketplace and growing your career alongside ambitious, supportive teams, we'd love to hear from you!

arbeitnow:mi-analyst-brighton-9352.description:
About Motorway

Motorway is the UK's largest online car-selling platform. We connect private sellers directly with over 8,000 dealers nationwide. Our online platform helps sellers achieve great prices for their cars while giving dealers fast, reliable access to the stock they want for their dealerships. Founded in 2017, our award-winning, technology-led approach has redefined the experience of selling a car. Motorway is backed by some of the world’s leading technology investors, having raised £143 million in Series C funding.

This is a unique opportunity to join a fast-growing scale-up at a crucial phase of growth and help change an industry for the better.

The role

As our MI Analyst, you will tell our Contact Centre leaders what the data means and what to do about it, then build the tools that deliver it at scale. You will sit in the Workforce Planning team, working across all teams who deal with customer contacts and report to the Head of Workforce Planning. Each day, week and month we publish reporting on agent productivity, operational performance and business review data across multiple teams and two sites. The job is to go beyond filling in the numbers and answer the "so what":

  • What are our most immediate opportunities?

  • What do we do about them with operational leaders?

  • Where are we losing efficiency?

  • Where could the same hours deliver more?

You will also use AI to do this faster than any manual process could. We run Claude connected to our BI data lake, so the right person can pull data, build reports and automate repeatable work themselves, without waiting in a queue. We want someone who sees that and immediately starts asking what they can automate.

What you will do

Find the insight

  • Turn Contact Centre data into clear findings and recommendations, and tell leaders what to do, not just what happened.

  • Spot where we are losing efficiency or capacity, size each opportunity, and prioritise the ones worth acting on.

  • Add commentary to the reports you publish, so readers see the story behind the numbers.

  • Own our understanding of contact drivers: explain why customers contact us, how that is changing, and what we could do to reduce it or handle it better.

Build with AI, at scale

  • Use Claude and our BI data lake to pull data, build reports and automate manual collation.

  • Replace repeatable, manual reporting with automated, reliable processes, so your time goes on analysis.

  • Bring us ideas for what to automate next, and show the time and capacity you save.

  • Document what you build so others in the team can run and maintain it when required.

Run the reporting cadence

  • Deliver daily, weekly and monthly reporting on agent productivity, utilisation and key service metrics across phone, email, chat and messaging.

  • Prepare the data for our daily, weekly and monthly business reviews (WBR and MBR).

  • Keep stakeholders updated on what you are working on and when it will land, without being asked.

Own accuracy

  • Validate every output before you share it. You are the last line of quality control on your own work.

  • Check sources and definitions rather than trusting historical reports, and flag anything that looks wrong before others find it.

  • Cross check your reports against the WBR and other sources, so mismatches show up before stakeholders spot them.

Be our Contact Centre data partner to BI

  • Act as the Contact Centre data partner to our BI teams, and the link between them and our operational leaders.

  • Help validate data models, dashboards and metrics against what is really happening on the floor.

  • Spot data issues early, raise them with BI with clear examples, and see them through to a fix.

  • Turn operational questions into clear requirements for BI, and help test what they build before it goes live.

  • Keep metric definitions consistent across Zendesk, Talkdesk, Calabrio and Looker.

Work with the business

  • Understand what team leaders and managers need from the data, and challenge whether our metrics are the right ones.

  • Help define and evolve Contact Centre KPIs as the business grows.

  • Support ad hoc analysis and reporting on test and learn initiatives, and on BPO partner performance.

What we are looking for

We want someone who has already worked with data in a busy operation and wants to do much more with it. If you are curious, thorough and keen to build, we want to hear from you.

You will need

  • Real curiosity about data. You ask why a number moved, not just what it is.

  • The ability to turn analysis into a clear recommendation that a non-technical leader can act on.

  • Strong attention to detail, and the habit of sense checking your own work before anyone else sees it.

  • Experience as an analyst, with a real understanding of the data you work with: where it comes from, how it is built, and what it can and cannot tell you.

  • Hands on experience using AI tools such as Claude to analyse data or build things, or a strong track record of picking up new tools fast.

  • Strong written and spoken communication, including working with BI teams to validate data and proactively updating stakeholders on progress and delays.

  • A drive to take ownership, without being prompted, of the reports and processes you run.

  • The ability to manage daily and weekly deadlines in a fast moving operation.

It would be great if you have

  • Experience in a Contact Centre or operations environment, and working knowledge of how AHT, occupancy, SLA and productivity are measured and what moves them.

  • Experience with BigQuery, dbt, Looker Studio or similar BI tools.

  • Experience with Zendesk, Talkdesk or Calabrio data.

  • Examples of something you automated or built that saved real time.

Why join us

  • Claude connected to our BI data lake, so you can build with real, live data from day one.

  • Your work is used every morning by operational leaders to run the day and directly impacts business performance.

  • Room to move from running reports to owning our Ops reporting automation.

  • A small team where good ideas get picked up and shipped.

Benefits

We've got your back, in life's biggest moments and the everyday ones too.

  • £34,000 per annum

  • Equity scheme - we all share in Motorway’s success

  • 33 days holiday (inclusive of bank holidays)

  • Sea-front office with bi-weekly massages and free snacks

  • Private medical insurance via BUPA

  • Life assurance

  • Pension scheme (we contribute 5%)

  • Enhanced family leave (e.g. 26 weeks full pay for maternity or adoption)

  • 24/7 Employee Assistance Programme

  • EV leasing scheme

  • Cycle to work scheme

  • Nursery salary sacrifice scheme

  • 1 paid volunteering day a year

Equal Opportunities Statement

Motorway is committed to equality of opportunity for all employees. We work to provide a supportive and inclusive environment where all individuals can maximise their full potential. We believe our workforce should reflect a variety of backgrounds, talents, perspectives and experiences. Our strong commitment to a culture of inclusion is evident through our constant focus on recruiting, developing and advancing individuals based on their skills and talents.

We welcome applications from all individuals regardless of age, disability, sex, gender reassignment, sexual orientation, pregnancy and maternity, race, religion or belief and marriage and civil partnerships.

arbeitnow:junior-python-software-enginee.description:
About Abound

We’re redefining consumer lending in the UK, and beyond. Using advanced AI and Open Banking data, we make fair, affordable personal finance available to more people. While traditional lenders rely almost entirely on credit scores, we look at the full financial picture - how much you spend, and what you can afford to repay to build a deeper, more accurate understanding of each customer's unique financial situation.


And we've shown it works at scale. We’ve issued over £1.3bn in loans directly to customers while delivering market-leading credit performance - for every 10 defaults the industry expects, we see only 3. We also reached profitability just 2.5 years after launch.


Backed by £2bn+ of funding from top-tier investors including Citi, GSR Ventures, and Deutsche Bank, we’re recognised as one of Europe’s fastest-growing fintechs (Sifted, CNBC). Now, we’re expanding into new markets and product lines - and we’re looking for ambitious people who want to learn fast, take ownership, and grow with us.

About the role

We’re looking for a Junior Software Engineer to join our New Products & Geographies Engineering team in London. This team launches and scales new lending propositions in two directions: bringing Abound’s lending to customers in new countries and expanding our B2B offering for partners. We move quickly, exploring ideas through production-ready MVPs and iterating as products mature.

This is a hybrid role, with at least three days a week in our London office. It’s a great opportunity for someone early in their career who wants to grow quickly, work on real production systems, and learn how a high-growth fintech operates from the inside.

You’ll work alongside experienced engineers who will support you through code reviews, pairing, and mentorship. We value engineers who are curious about the business and are keen to work with stakeholders to improve processes and customer experience.

Our technology stack

Python (including FastAPI, OpenTelemetry, procrastinate, SQLAlchemy and Uvicorn), Postgres, MySQL, Liquibase, Retool, Docker and AWS.

What you’ll be doing:

  • Build and maintain features in our backend services, which can span any part of the lending lifecycle – from finding and onboarding new customers, to helping underwriters assess affordability, through to paying out and collecting loans

  • Take part in the full software development lifecycle: contributing to designs, writing tests, reviewing code and helping with deployments

  • Write clean, well-tested Python, with guidance and feedback from senior engineers

  • Work with colleagues in Product and Design, as well as internal users, to understand requirements and turn them into working software

  • Work closely with our React frontend developers to build the APIs and backend logic their features rely on

  • Write and improve SQL queries against our Postgres databases

  • Help troubleshoot and resolve system issues that affect our customers

  • Gradually take ownership of parts of the platform as your experience grows

Who you are:

You’ll need:

  • 0–2 years of professional software engineering experience, or equivalent experience from a degree, bootcamp, internships or personal projects

  • Working knowledge of Python – you don’t need to be an expert, but you’re comfortable writing, testing and debugging code

  • An understanding of core programming concepts such as data structures, object-oriented design and unit testing

  • Familiarity with SQL, relational databases and Git

  • To be able to work from our London office at least three days a week

You’ll do well here if you:

  • Have a sharp eye for detail – in lending, small mistakes can have a real impact on customers

  • Learn quickly, take initiative and work methodically through problems, even in a large, evolving codebase

  • Communicate clearly, ask questions, take on feedback and work well in a team

  • Have a genuine interest in fintech and how financial products work

Ideally you'll also have:

  • Experience with async Python or frameworks such as FastAPI

  • Basic familiarity with cloud platforms (AWS, GCP or Azure) or Docker

  • Knowledge of lending products or open banking

How we work:

To be successful here, our culture needs to energies you. Here’s how we operate:

  • High bar and real ownership: We’re a high-performing team, and we hire people who raise the bar and take pride in great work. We own outcomes, not tasks.

  • Focus on impact: We measure success by what we deliver to customers. We prioritise carefully so our energy goes where it makes the biggest difference.

  • MVP and iteration culture: We ship fast, learn from real customers, and continuously improve our products and processes.

  • One team collaboration: We collaborate closely across engineering, product, operations and the wider business.

  • Thrive in change: Priorities evolve as we learn what works. We value people who use good judgement, adapt quickly, and stay focused on outcomes.

What we offer:

  • Equity – everyone owns a piece of the company

  • Hybrid working, with three days a week in the office

  • 25 days’ holiday a year, plus 8 bank holidays

  • 2 paid volunteering days a year

  • A one-month paid sabbatical after 4 years

  • Employee loan

  • Free gym membership through WellHub

  • A team wellness budget to be active together – set up a yoga class, a tennis lesson or go bouldering

🚀 Why Midnite?

Midnite is a next-generation sports betting and gaming platform built for a new wave of players.

We combine sharp product thinking, bold brand, and fast execution to create experiences that feel modern, intuitive, and built for how people actually play today.

Over 400,000 players have already made the move, and we’re only just getting started.

We’re a high-performance team operating at pace. High ownership. Constant iteration. No hiding behind processes. We move quickly, test relentlessly, and turn ambitious ideas into real impact. If you’re driven, creative, and thrive in fast-moving environments where you can shape meaningful outcomes - keep reading.

Not your grandad’s bookie.

The Sports Group owns Midnite’s sportsbook experience - from discovering sports and markets to building, placing and tracking bets, cashing out and settlement. We build customer-facing products, critical backend services and the trading and operational tools that power them, working closely with Product, Design and Trading to expand our sports offering and make complex, real-time betting systems feel simple, fast and reliable. Within the group, the Sportsbook Platform team is modernising the tools behind that experience through an improved back office and practical use of AI, helping our trading team work more efficiently, reduce manual effort and gain greater control over the sportsbook.

 

We’re looking for an Engineering Lead to provide hands-on technical leadership while formally managing and developing a team of three to four engineers. This is not a conventional Engineering Manager role or a purely technical lead position: you’ll create PRs, write production code and release features while setting technical direction and helping the whole team perform at its best.

 

You’ll bring deep backend experience and a full-stack, systems-thinking mindset, understanding how clients, APIs, services, data, infrastructure, operations and third-party integrations work together. You’ll work closely with Product, Design and the trading team to turn complex or ambiguous problems into simple, reliable experiences delivered incrementally. Your impact will be measured not only by what you build, but by the quality of the team’s technical decisions, delivery and growth.

 

You will:

  • Technical direction: Set pragmatic technical direction and lead system design across clients, APIs, services, data, infrastructure and integrations.

  • Hands-on engineering: Create PRs, write production code and release features, alongside contributing technical designs, investigations and reviews.

  • Product delivery: Work with Product and Design to turn ambiguous opportunities into clear milestones, small deliverables and frequent releases.

  • People leadership: Manage three to four engineers through clear expectations, one-to-ones, feedback, performance management and development support.

  • Coaching: Develop engineers through design discussions, reviews, pairing, debugging and production incidents without becoming a bottleneck.

  • Engineering quality: Champion effective testing, observability, safe releases and strong production feedback loops.

  • Technical judgement: Make sensible trade-offs, keep risks visible and help the team improve systems following production problems.

  • Wider contribution: Use AI responsibly and contribute to hiring, onboarding and shared engineering practices.

 

The next Midniter:

  • Significant backend engineering experience, including time operating at senior or lead level.

  • Deep backend expertise with a full-stack, systems-thinking mindset across clients, APIs, services, data, infrastructure and operations.

  • Strong Python skills, or experience with another modern backend language and a willingness to learn Python.

  • Experience setting technical direction and designing, delivering and operating reliable systems.

  • Experience in formally managing engineers, or strong evidence of readiness to own one-to-ones, feedback, performance and development for a team of three to four.

  • Challenge assumptions constructively, helping Product and Design find simpler or more effective ways to achieve the intended outcome and the ability to break ambiguous, complex work into simple, safe deliverables.

  • Solid database and production-engineering fundamentals, including AWS, CI/CD and observability.

  • You communicate with energy and clarity, bring others into technical discussions, and help create momentum across the team.

 

💰 Winnings

  • Private health insurance with zero excess, including optical cover and optional dental.

  • Income protection to protect your earnings and give you peace of mind.

arbeitnow:engineering-lead-security-lond.description:
About 9fin

9fin is the AI platform powering global debt markets — the world’s largest asset class at over $145 trillion.

Debt markets are vast, global, and mission-critical, yet still run on fragmented data, PDFs, and manual workflows. 9fin replaces this broken infrastructure with a single platform that centralises proprietary credit data, deep analysis, and high-value workflows across global markets.

Today, 9fin powers teams at 300+ blue-chip institutions worldwide, including global banks, asset managers, private equity firms, law firms, and advisors. The business is scaling at exceptional speed, with rapid expansion in the US and best-in-class retention driven by deep workflow adoption.

We’re at a defining inflection point. With proven product-market fit and strong, global market pull, 9fin is accelerating toward becoming the category-defining platform for debt markets worldwide.

The role

We’re hiring a Security Engineering Lead to build and lead our security engineering team, reporting to the Head of Platform.

You’ll manage engineers working across product and platform security, set a clear direction for the function and help us grow our product security capability. You’ll join a small team with both specialisms already represented and shape how it develops.

Our product security engineers work alongside Product Engineering teams, contributing to planning, design, code and delivery. They report to you for technical development, performance and career progression. You’ll stay close enough to their work to support them well, even when you are not part of their day-to-day team.

You’ll bring experience as a security engineer and as a people manager. You should be able to challenge a design, reason through a threat model and help an engineer find a practical solution. You’ll also need to make choices about where we invest, build relationships across engineering and explain security priorities in terms of customer and business risk.

What you’ll do

  • Lead and develop our product and platform security engineers through regular feedback, coaching, clear expectations and fair performance assessment.

  • Build a focused security engineering strategy and roadmap, informed by our products, engineering plans and the risks that matter most.

  • Grow the team thoughtfully, identifying capability gaps and taking responsibility for hiring and onboarding.

  • Agree sustained product security placements with engineering leaders, with clear priorities, useful feedback and a strong connection to the security team.

  • Help teams build security into architecture and implementation, including access control, tenant isolation, confidential data handling and AI systems.

  • Work with Platform Engineering to make secure infrastructure and delivery practices easy to adopt, using shared controls and automation where they help.

  • Stay involved in important technical decisions through design and code reviews, investigations and selective implementation.

  • Help engineers raise concerns and resolve disagreements constructively. Make material risks and trade-offs clear to the leaders accountable for the decision.

  • Partner with IT and Information Security on shared risks, incident response and assurance requirements.

  • Measure whether our approach reduces meaningful risk and helps engineers deliver securely. Use what we learn to improve it.


What we’re looking for

  • A background in hands-on security engineering, with strong product or application security experience.

  • Demonstrated line management experience: developing engineers, giving difficult feedback, assessing performance and supporting career progression.

  • Experience supporting engineers whose daily work happens within other teams, or comparable evidence of managing effectively without observing all their work directly.

  • Current technical judgement across secure software design, threat modelling, authentication, authorisation and protection of sensitive data.

  • Enough cloud and platform security breadth to guide specialists and make sound decisions across both areas.

  • Experience setting priorities and securing support for security improvements across engineering teams.

  • The ability to explain risk clearly, offer workable options and make proportionate recommendations under uncertainty.

  • A collaborative approach that helps product and platform engineers own the security of the systems they build.

You should be comfortable reading and reviewing production code and discussing implementation choices. The role combines technical leadership with people management and responsibility for building the function.


Useful experience

  • Working with AWS, backend services, infrastructure as code and automated delivery.

  • Securing multi-tenant products, confidential customer data or AI-enabled systems.

  • Building or improving a small security engineering team in a growing organisation.

  • Introducing secure patterns or tooling that engineers adopted and continued to use.

We value evidence of sound judgement and useful outcomes. You do not need experience with every technology we use.

What success looks like

During your first months, you’ll understand the team’s strengths, our main risks and how security work gets done. You’ll agree development plans with the engineers and establish clear working relationships with Product Engineering, Platform and Information Security.

Over the following months, you’ll put a prioritised roadmap and a workable embedded model in place. Teams should involve security earlier in important decisions, engineers should have useful technical support, and the highest-priority improvements should have clear owners and delivery capacity.

As the function grows, we’ll look for evidence of better protection for customers, adoption of secure engineering practices and a team whose engineers are developing in their roles.

Hybrid Policy

9fin is a hybrid company, and the office is a regular part of how we work. From January 2027, all employees will work from their designated 9fin office on Tuesdays and Wednesdays. Some teams may be asked to be in the office more often, where the nature of their work calls for it. For the rest of the week, you may work from wherever works best for you and your team. Your Talent Partner will share hybrid working details for this role.

We recognize that building diverse teams enables a more creative and productive environment. arbeitnow:solutions-engineer-london-1202.description:
We’re Making Travel Effortless. Join Us.

Travel is essential, whether it’s visiting family, starting a new adventure, or taking a career defining trip. Yet today, over 4 billion airline passengers rely on tech that hasn't changed in decades.

At Duffel, we’re rebuilding the infrastructure underpinning the global travel industry. Backed by top-tier investors (Benchmark, Blossom, Index Ventures, and Kima Ventures) and born out of Y Combinator (S18), we’re simplifying complex systems to build the future of travel.

Customer Success at Duffel

Customer Success owns Duffel's relationship with our customers once the contract is signed. We help them integrate, launch and grow on Duffel across Flights, Stays and more. The team brings together Customer Success Managers, Customer Success Engineers and Technical Support Engineers across London and New York, led by our VP, Customer Success. We're growing the team and building the processes that help customers go live faster and get more from Duffel.

The Role

We're hiring a Solutions Engineer: the technical expert who helps customers design the right Duffel solution during the sales process, then guides them through building it until they go live.

In pre-sales, you'll join our Account Executives on discovery calls and pitches, bringing the technical depth to understand how a customer's product works and design how Duffel fits into it. Once the deal is signed, you'll take that design into implementation as the customer's technical point of contact, making sure they go live smoothly with the best setup for their use case.

This is a senior individual contributor role reporting to the VP, Customer Success. You'll be our first Solutions Engineer, so the way you do this job will become how the team works as it grows. That could lead to managing a team of solutions engineers, or to a principal-level technical role shaping how our largest customers build on Duffel. Most of our transaction volume is in the US, so you'll work closely with US-based customer teams from London.

What You’ll be doing:

  • Join Account Executives on discovery calls, pitches and technical deep-dives, running technical discovery on the customer's product, architecture, user journeys and travel use case.

  • Design the solution, build demos and proofs of concept, and write solution designs and implementation scopes so customers know what they're building before they sign. Answer technical questions in RFPs and security reviews.

  • Take what you designed into implementation as the customer's technical point of contact: answer their engineers' questions, review integrations, define test plans and run go-live readiness checks.

  • Debug integration issues hands-on with Postman or curl and our API logs, working alongside the Senior Implementation Project Manager, who owns the project plan and dates.

  • Feed integration friction back to Product and Engineering, build reusable assets such as solution templates, sample code and demo apps, and define how pre-sales and implementation run at Duffel.

What we're looking for:

  • 5+ years in a customer-facing technical role, such as solutions engineer, sales engineer, implementation engineer or technical account manager, at an API-first company.

  • Experience on both sides of the contract: supporting sales with discovery, demos and solution design, then implementing what was sold and taking enterprise customers live on complex integrations.

  • Hands-on API skills (REST, JSON, webhooks, authentication, sandbox vs production) and enough coding in a language such as JavaScript, Python, PHP, Ruby or Java to build a demo and spot what's wrong in a customer's integration.

  • The ability to explain a solution clearly to engineers and commercial decision-makers in the same meeting, and sound judgement on when to push back on a custom request or bring in Product.

Fuse Energy is an energy startup on a mission to make energy abundant and affordable, fast. We combine first-principles thinking with cutting-edge technology to build a radically better energy system.

We've raised over $200M from top-tier investors including Balderton, Lakestar, Accel, Creandum, Lowercarbon, Ribbit, 20VC, Hummingbird and Collaborative Fund, alongside strategic angels including Nico Rosberg and GPs behind Meta, Revolut, Spotify and Uber.

We're building a fully integrated energy company: developing our own solar, batteries and other generation projects, building our own hardware, improving and developing grid infrastructure, trading power in real time, using AI across the business, and installing distributed energy in homes. By selling directly to consumers we cut out the middleman, lower costs and pass the savings on to our customers.

As a Brand designer, you own how Fuse looks. You take our new identity, Fuse Brand 2.0, and turn it into a system the whole company can use, then carry it into everything we put into the world: national campaigns, billboards and TV ads, the website and app, merch, engineer uniforms and vans, and the hardware we build. With a new identity landing and launches every month, few brands will give you this much to define.

What you'll do

  • Build and own the Fuse visual identity system: type, colour, photography, illustration, layout, and how they flex from a sticker to a billboard
  • Write the guidelines and templates that let creators, producers and agencies stay on brand without you in the room
  • Design the big brand moments yourself: campaign identities, out of home, launches, packaging, merch, uniforms and van livery
  • Art direct the look of shoots and work with motion, graphic design and our agency partners so everything feels like one brand
  • Hold the bar on every piece of work that carries the Fuse name, and evolve the brand as we expand into new countries and products

Requirements

Two things matter most:

Taste. You have a distinct eye and a strong point of view, and you can build a visual world that looks like nobody else's. Everything you make feels considered, right down to the type.

Thinking. You start from the idea. You can take a strategy and a belief and turn them into a system with a reason behind every choice, and you can explain those reasons in plain words to anyone in the company.

Beyond that, we want someone with deep craft in typography, colour and composition, who has built or evolved an identity system that went live in the real world, and who moves fast without letting quality slip. We expect you to have 5+ years experience, ideally at a top studio or on an in-house team at a brand people admire. Motion, 3D or packaging experience is a bonus.

Benefits

  • Competitive salary and eligibility for equity
  • Biannual bonus scheme
  • Fully expensed tech to match your needs
  • Private health insurance
  • Breakfast and dinner allowance for office-based employees

arbeitnow:founding-product-manager-claap.description:
we're hiring our first PM at Claap. You'll own the core product across three big topics in-app agentic experience, off-app agentic experience and enterprise readiness working directly with Robin, our co-founder and CEO.

About Claap

Claap is the AI-native Revenue Intelligence platform for sales and revenue teams.

What makes us different: we were the first platform in our category designed from day one to be used by both humans AND AI agents. We were also the first in our category to release an MCP, back in May 2025, over 18 months ago. Every customer conversation we capture is structured for two consumers: the rep who needs to act on it, and the agents (yours, ours, third-party) that need to feed on it to do their work.

This matters because the biggest shift we see across our customer base, from Series B startups to enterprise customers like Infopro Digital, Didomi, Dash0, and Pelico, is the move toward collaboration between humans, agents, and software. Our customers' executives are under real pressure to deploy AI across sales, business development, and customer-facing functions. Claap is often the conversation-data backbone that makes those agentic workflows possible.

Claap is now part of lempire (lemlist), giving us the ambition to build the agentic revenue platform (from prospection to closing) of the next decade.

We're a small team. Every hire matters and we are looking for our 1st PM.

As the first Product Manager at Claap, your mission is to drive the product's future developments and roadmap, working hand in hand with Robin, our co-founder and CEO, who has led product since day one.

You will work with Robin on three big topics:

- In-app agentic experience: In the past few months, we have extended our context infra. We now need to put this context at work to truly move the needle for our sales clients and help them close faster. Think next best action for the sales rep (prep meeting, build decks, contact people, follow ups & co), assisted pipeline reviews & forecasts or sales coaching.

- Off-app agentic experience: Claap is becoming headless, consumed more and more through MCP. We now need to level up our MCP integrations to make Claap fully sticky and efficient through MCP usage in 3rd party agents. Think MCP tools, plugins, embed skills or Claude artifact app.

- Enterprise readiness: our customers are moving upmarket, and enterprise accounts need governance, admin settings, permissions and configuration capabilities to roll Claap out at scale. Think SSO/SCIM, roles and permissions, data retention policies, and admin analytics.

The lemlist integration and our end-to-end sales agent roadmap will stay with Robin, which leaves you real ownership on the core Claap product (ie closing).

Your role is to understand the market and customer needs (especially in this AI era), identify the best possible product evolutions, prioritize them, work hand-in-hand with developers and designers to build an amazing product experience, and have a strong focus on go-to-market with Sales and Marketing to make sure the impact is reached.

Your scope can change over time; we are a truly agile company: we iterate a lot, even on how we organize and work together.

The PM at Claap wears different hats

- A detective/explorer hat to find unusual insights & opportunities, read between the lines of what sales teams really need, and be visionary when needed

- A chess player hat to think strategically, create good decision constraints, double down on the right things, and always have a coup d'avance

- An investor hat to make the right bets at the right time with the right amount of resources, because you sometimes need to play fast and risky, and sometimes need to play safe

- A diplomat hat to influence your teammates on what we should spend time and effort on, win their trust, and bring visibility, focus, vision and motivation

- A builder hat to get your hands dirty with AI, prototype, test and ship, instead of only writing specs about it

What you are not

- A Project Manager who only talks about methodologies and frameworks

- A Product Owner writing super detailed 4-page tickets for devs

- A feature factory building every custom request an enterprise prospect asks for

- The "Notion docs & meetings person" with no real impact on our users and the business

- A "yes man" for every idea and suggestion people bring to you

- A people manager looking for a team to run: this role is hands-on

Key results

Within 3 months you will have

- Developed a deep understanding of Claap, the call intelligence market and our product vision

- Built relationships with Claap users, from sales reps to the admins of our largest accounts

  • Satisfaction: set up and follow NPS campaigns.

  • Adoption: run campaigns to increase usage of Parallel across our customers.

  • Product feedback: share what you see in the field and work with Product on levers to increase usage.

  • Management: manage two experienced people, set the framework and priorities, help them grow and structure the team as the number of accounts increases.

Who you are

  • You have 3 to 5 years of experience in Customer Success, with your own B2B customer portfolio.

  • You have already managed people, even an intern, and you have the credibility to lead two experienced people.

  • You have already set up NPS campaigns and done account monitoring: you know which indicators you track and how you detect an account in trouble.

  • You make decisions on your own on an account and raise the alarm when a metric drops.

  • You want to keep working directly on accounts on top of managing: this is not a pure management role.

  • A plus: experience with key account portfolios.

Our values

  • Play to Win: we're not here to just take part, deliver something "good enough" or simply enjoy the startup ride. We want to win. That means caring about results, moving fast and bringing the right intensity when it matters.

  • High Trust, High Standards: trust is our starting point. If you join us, it's because we believe you can own your scope and make good decisions.   • Real traction: seed and Series A ($20M with Index Ventures) closed in less than a year, more than 800 clients and a team of over 30 people.

  • Strong investors and founders: Index Ventures, Y Combinator, Hexa, Frst, Kima Ventures, Better Angle and the CEO of Mistral AI; founders who come from Meta, McKinsey and Hublo.

À propos de Lexroom

Chez Lexroom, nous développons l'état de l'art de la recherche juridique agentique. Notre plateforme décompose chaque question juridique en sous-questions précises, puis mobilise des agents spécialisés pour explorer en parallèle les codes, jurisprudences, doctrines et textes européens. Chaque source est minutieusement analysée, les liens implicites entre principes sont identifiés, et toutes les informations sont synthétisées dans un rapport structuré, avec chaque affirmation soigneusement sourcée. Ce qui, auparavant, demandait une semaine à une équipe se réalise désormais pendant une pause café.

Notre mission : rendre le droit plus rapide, plus clair et plus fiable, afin que les avocats et les directions juridiques puissent se concentrer sur l'essentiel.

Nous construisons l'équipe commerciale en France, et nous cherchons la personne qui va la former, l'accompagner et la faire monter en compétence à travers la Lexroom Sales Academy.

Pourquoi rejoindre Lexroom ?

  • Un produit qui tient ses promesses : nos démos sont impactantes et convainquent dès la première session, pas besoin de six mois de POC.

  • Un marché en pleine effervescence : tous les cabinets français recherchent une solution IA, et les usages sont encore à inventer.

  • Un avantage concurrentiel fort : vous ne formez pas des commerciaux à vendre un assistant IA de plus, mais une approche radicalement nouvelle que les prospects n'ont jamais vue.

  • Un impact direct : la qualité de l'équipe commerciale française dépendra de ce que vous construisez.

Vos responsabilités

  • Piloter la Lexroom Sales Academy en France : concevoir et animer des programmes de formation récurrents (onboarding, ramp-up, formation avancée), avec objectifs, contenus, calendrier et indicateurs de succès.

  • Gérer l'onboarding des nouvelles recrues commerciales : première semaine et deux premiers mois de ramp-up, en coordonnant agendas, supports, intervenants internes et exercices pratiques.

  • Animer vous-même les modules de formation : méthodologie de vente, discovery, démos, traitement des objections, négociation, gestion du pipeline, avec role-plays, coaching sur les appels et feedback structuré.

  • Maintenir les contenus à jour : playbooks, scripts, templates et supports de l'Academy, en phase avec l'évolution du produit, du marché et des performances de l'équipe. Transformer les succès internes (appels, emails, séquences, deals complexes) en ressources de formation réutilisables.

  • Travailler main dans la main avec les Sales Managers et les AE pour que la formation se traduise concrètement dans le pipeline, les appels et les démos.

  • Aligner l'Academy France avec les initiatives globales et adapter au marché français les best practices déjà éprouvées en Italie.

Profil recherché

  • Expérience en management commercial, sales enablement ou gestion de projet en environnement B2B (idéalement SaaS, tech ou conseil).

  • Solide mindset PMO : capacité à transformer des besoins en plans structurés, aligner les parties prenantes, tenir les délais, livrer et mesurer l'impact.

  • À l'aise aussi bien en animation (formations, ateliers, role-plays) que dans le travail de détail sur les process, les contenus et les métriques.

  • Excellentes compétences en communication, résolution de problèmes et collaboration transverse.

  • Très opérationnel : vous ne vous contentez pas de concevoir des programmes, vous participez aux appels, analysez les chiffres et itérez vite.

  • Français natif, anglais courant (équipes internes internationales).

  • Intérêt pour le droit : une expérience dans le secteur juridique ou des services professionnels est un plus, mais pas indispensable.

Ce que nous offrons

  • Rémunération fixe: 80 k€ brut annuel + variable sur objectifs

  • Equity

  • Mutuelle Alan, titres-restaurant, accès Wellpass (sport et bien-être)

  • Travail hybride, bureaux à Paris

  • Team retreats et off-sites

  3. Mise en situation : conception et animation d'un module de formation.

Vous êtes passionné(e) par le développement des énergies renouvelables et vous connaissez bien le tissu économique et territorial de l’Est de la France ? Rejoignez Novar et devenez un acteur clé de la transition énergétique !

Vos missions

·         Assurer une veille active des opportunités de marché (appels à projets, appels d’offres) sur votre territoire.

·         Construire et maintenir un réseau local solide, incluant partenaires, collectivités et apporteurs d’affaires.

·         Réaliser l’analyse technico-économique des sites, en intégrant contraintes et risques.

·         Approcher les propriétaires fonciers, agriculteurs, collectivités et clients C&I afin de présenter Novar et ses solutions.

·         Préparer et présenter des réponses à des appels à projets.

·         Négocier et contractualiser les accords fonciers et commerciaux.

·         Assurer le suivi des opportunités jusqu’à leur concrétisation et leur passage en phase de développement.

arbeitnow:cdi-designer-junior-jersey-h-f.description:
LA MAISON JACQUEMUS
 
Jacquemus a été fondée par Simon Porte Jacquemus en 2009 à Paris, en France.
Dédiée à la mémoire de la mère du créateur, la marque puise son inspiration dans une passion pour la culture. Les collections femme et homme font référence à l'art de vivre à la française et aux gestes universels de beauté, intégrant des influences allant de la photographie d'art aux arts décoratifs, en passant par le cinéma, la peinture et la sculpture.
 
Au fil des années, Jacquemus a mis en scène ses défilés dans des lieux uniques et inattendus, notamment une piscine parisienne, le Musée Picasso, un champ de lavande en Provence, un champ de blé aux abords de Paris, un marais salant en Camargue et une plage à Hawaï. Plus récemment, la marque a investi des lieux tels que le canal du Château de Versailles (Le Chouchou), la Fondation Maeght (Les Sculptures), la Casa Malaparte (La Casa) et l'appartement parisien d'Auguste Perret (La Croisière).
 
Basé dans le 8ᵉ arrondissement de Paris, Jacquemus est une maison de mode indépendante comptant plus de 300 employés. Réputée pour sa forte présence numérique et son expansion internationale, la marque a développé des expériences de vente innovantes à travers le monde avant d'ouvrir son premier flagship permanent au 58 Avenue Montaigne à Paris en 2022. Depuis, des boutiques ont été ouvertes à New York (SoHo) et Londres (New Bond Street).
 
 
 
VOTRE ROLE

Rattaché(e) à la Head of Design, vous intervenez sur la création des collections homme et femme, jersey, bain et flou show, des recherches d'images jusqu'au suivi des prototypes en normalisation.
Ce poste couvre à la fois la création et le développement produit : vous travaillez en lien avec les usines partenaires et participez au bien aller de chaque pièce.

 

VOS MISSIONS

  • Réaliser les recherches iconographiques et construire les boards de collection
  • Mener les recherches de volumes, de finitions et de graphismes
  • Réaliser les visuels sur Photoshop et les maquettes
  • Assurer le sourcing matière
  • Établir les fiches de lancement et suivre les corrections de prototypes
  • Réaliser les dessins techniques
  • Participer aux essayages
  • Accompagner les pièces jusqu'à la normalisation, en lien avec les usines
 
 
VOTRE PROFIL

Vous justifiez d'une première expérience d'environ 2 ans en tant que designer junior, idéalement sur le jersey et/ou le flou.

Vous avez également :

  • Une sensibilité forte pour le bien aller du vêtement, avec un attrait pour le flou et le travail en 3D
  • La maîtrise de la suite Adobe (Photoshop, Illustrator, InDesign) et une aisance en dessin technique
  • Un esprit autonome, débrouillard et force de proposition
  • La capacité à prendre rapidement des automatismes et à gérer plusieurs sujets en parallèle
  • L'envie d'évoluer au sein d'un studio créatif exigeant
 
 
Le poste est basé à Paris dans le 8ème arrondissement

🚲Derrière chaque piste cyclable pérennisée, chaque site naturel préservé, il y a une décision. Et derrière cette décision, il y a nos données.

Chez Eco-Compteur, nous aidons les villes et les gestionnaires d’espaces naturels à décider sur des faits, pas à l’intuition.

Nos capteurs connectés mesurent la fréquentation piétons et cyclistes, en ville comme en pleine nature, et nos logiciels transforment ces données en indicateurs concrets : impact d’un aménagement, évolution de la pratique, effet des saisons. Parce que compter, c’est bien, mais donner du sens aux chiffres, c’est encore mieux !

🌍 Pionniers et leader mondial d’un métier que nous avons créé il y a plus de 20 ans, nous sommes basés en Bretagne, avec des filiales sur quatre continents et des solutions présentes dans plus de 55 pays.

🤝 Une entreprise à taille humaine, portée par l’autonomie, la responsabilité et la transparence, avec beaucoup de passion (et de plaisir !).

Envie que vos compétences aient un impact concret ? Nous recherchons notre prochain·e :

Stage de fin d’études · 6 mois · Lannion (22)

Nous préparons un nouveau banc de test capable de piloter une dizaine de produits différents. Chaque produit sera relié à une carte de pilotage qui gère ses interfaces, son alimentation et la mesure de sa consommation. Un poste central dialogue ensuite avec chacune de ces cartes pour dérouler les tests et scénarios attendus.

Le défi : router les bons bus vers le bon produit selon le test en cours (USB, UART, I2C, JTAG, …), et pouvoir déconnecter physiquement les équipements pour mesurer la consommation sans perturbation.

Tu utiliseras Claude (IA) au quotidien pour t’aider dans la conception, le développement et la documentation.

 

✏️Tes rôles :

– Recenser les besoins de test des produits (interfaces, séquences, mesures) et définir l’architecture du banc

– Concevoir la carte de pilotage (schéma, routage, mise au point) : commutation des bus, déconnexion physique des équipements, alimentation et mesure de consommation (précision, calibration, asservissement)

– Développer son firmware et le protocole de communication avec le poste central

– Développer le logiciel de supervision qui pilote chaque carte et déroule les scénarios de test

– Intégrer le banc à notre chaîne CI/CD (Jenkins, Git) pour lancer les tests automatiquement

– Valider le banc sur les produits, documenter et le mettre en service

Le poste est basé à Lannion, Bretagne, au sein d’une technopole à taille humaine d’envergure mondiale (1er centre R&D Orange Labs en France et 2ème site Nokia français). Les loisirs, nautiques notamment, sont particulièrement accessibles par la localisation à 5 km de la Côte de Granit Rose

Ce que l’on te met à disposition :

  • Des outils performants qui permettront d’exprimer pleinement tes talents

  • Une équipe de passionnés qui travaillera à tes côtés


👉Et si c’était toi ?

– Bac+5, école d’ingénieur ou master en électronique / systèmes embarqués

– Électronique numérique : bus UART, I2C, JTAG, conception de cartes

– Firmware embarqué en C sur microcontrôleur

– Bases en mesure de courant, alimentation et asservissement

– Python pour la supervision et l’automatisation des tests, Git, CI/CD (Jenkins)

– Curieux(se), autonome, rigoureux(se), à l’aise en laboratoire

L’entreprise et le projet te plaisent ?

« il ne faut jamais remettre au lendemain ce qu'on peut faire le jour-même » : Tu n’es pas arrivé.e jusqu’ici pour postuler « plus tard » ! C’est rapide, ça prend 2 minutes (et c’est vrai !)

  • Rédiger les réponses aux appels d'offres publics et privés (dont le mémoire technique), en t'appuyant sur les équipes internes.
