Dies ist praktische, wirtschaftlich substanzielle Arbeit. Sie werden direkt den Unterschied sehen, den Sie in messbaren Ergebnissen, stärkeren Unternehmen und selbstbewussteren Eigentümern machen.

Gleichzeitig bauen Sie eine angesehene lokale Beratung mit wiederkehrenden Kundenbeziehungen, geringen Betriebskosten und dem Potenzial auf, langfristiges, skalierbares Einkommen und Wert zu schaffen.

Die Gelegenheit

Sie werden die Unabhängigkeit haben, Ihr eigenes Unternehmen auf- und auszubauen, unterstützt durch:

  • Eine bewährte Mentoring- und Wachstumsmethodik für KMU

  • Eine etablierte internationale Marke

  • Drei Wochen strukturiertes Kerntraining

  • Eins-zu-eins-Coaching in der Anlaufphase

  • Zugang zu internationalen Best Practices

  • Ein professionelles Peer-Netzwerk erfahrener Partner

Sie werden ein bewährtes Modell anwenden und gleichzeitig Ihr eigenes Urteilsvermögen, Ihre Erfahrung und Ihre Beziehungen ins Unternehmen einbringen.

Wer Sie sind

Sie sind eine leitende Führungskraft, Geschäftsinhaber oder erfahrener Berater mit mindestens 12 Jahren Erfahrung in unternehmerischen Positionen mit Substanz.

Sie werden in mindestens zwei der folgenden Bereiche umfassende Erfahrung haben:

  • Strategie und Geschäftsentwicklung

  • Finanzen und kommerzielles Management

  • Vertrieb und Marketing

  • Operative und organisatorische Führung

  • Managementberatung

Noch wichtiger ist, dass Sie denken und handeln werden wie ein Unternehmensinhaber.

Sie haben außerdem ein echtes Interesse daran, Unternehmen und ihren Eigentümern zum Erfolg zu verhelfen, anstatt nur ein standardisiertes Beratungsrahmen bereitzustellen.

Bewerbung

Wenn dies der nächste Schritt ist, den Sie in Betracht ziehen, bewerben Sie sich bitte mit Ihrem Lebenslauf und einer kurzen Notiz, in der Sie erläutern, was Sie in dieser Phase Ihrer Karriere an dieser Gelegenheit anzieht.

Über EVEREST

EVEREST ist Ideengeber und Projektentwickler für digitale Tools, die Gründer*innen und Kleinunternehmer*innen Zugang zu wirtschaftlichem Know-how, Kapital und Ressourcen ermöglichen. Wir entwickeln Empowerment-Plattformen von der Konzeption bis zum Betrieb – z.B. die kostenlose bundesweite Gründerplattform oder das digitale Beratungsprogramm InStart für Soloselbstständige und Kleinunternehmen in der Krise in Hamburg. Deren Nutzer*innen haben Zugang zu ständig aktualisiertem Wissen, können ihre eigenen unternehmerischen Pläne umsetzen, wichtige Kontakte knüpfen und als Community voneinander profitieren.

Zur Verstärkung unseres Teams am Standort Hamburg-Altstadt suchen wir dich in Vollzeit oder Teilzeit für eine befristete Position als:

Senior Product Owner (m/w/d) – Digitale Startup-Plattform

Das erwartet dich

Eine gute digitale Anwendung macht komplizierte Dinge einfach. Genau daran arbeitest du bei uns.

Wir entwickeln ein neues digitales Plattformprojekt rund um die Themen Gründung und Startups. Dahinter stehen verschiedene Teilprojekte, komplexe fachliche Anforderungen und viele Ideen, die sinnvoll miteinander verbunden werden müssen.

Als Senior Product Owner sorgst du dafür, dass aus diesen Ideen ein durchdachtes, technisch realisierbares und vor allem nutzerfreundliches Produkt entsteht.

Du arbeitest eng mit der Geschäftsführung, Projektleitung und unserem Entwicklungsteam zusammen. Dabei erwarten wir, dass du Entscheidungen fachlich hinterfragst, Abhängigkeiten erkennst und eigene Lösungsvorschläge einbringst.


Deine Aufgaben

  • Produktentwicklung steuern: Du behältst die verschiedenen Teilprojekte im Blick, erkennst Abhängigkeiten und sorgst dafür, dass Funktionen in einer sinnvollen Reihenfolge entwickelt werden.

  • Entscheidungen fundiert vorbereiten: Du prüfst Ideen und Anforderungen auf Nutzen, Logik und technische Machbarkeit. Wenn ein geplanter Entwicklungsschritt noch nicht sinnvoll ist, erklärst du, warum das so ist, und zeigst Alternativen auf.

  • Komplexität für Nutzer*innen reduzieren: Du übersetzt komplexes Expertenwissen rund um Gründungsprozesse in einfache, intuitive digitale Anwendungen. Dabei berücksichtigst du die unterschiedlichen Bedürfnisse und Herausforderungen von Gründerinnen – von der ersten Geschäftsidee über die Gründung bis hin zum Wachstum. Dein Anspruch: Nutzerinnen finden in jeder Phase die passende Unterstützung, ohne selbst Expert*innen sein zu müssen.

  • Nutzererlebnisse konzipieren: Du entwickelst mit Figma eigenständig User Flows, Wireframes und interaktive Prototypen, überprüfst Konzepte anhand von Nutzerfeedback und optimierst sie gemeinsam mit dem Team.

  • Entwicklung konkret voranbringen: Du übersetzt Anforderungen in verständliche User Stories und Entwicklungstickets, priorisierst das Product Backlog und klärst fachliche Fragen direkt mit dem Entwicklungsteam.

  • Roadmap und Qualität im Blick behalten: Gemeinsam mit Geschäftsführung und Projektleitung planst du realistische Entwicklungsschritte, begleitest neue Funktionen bis zum Go-live und nutzt Feedback und KPIs für die weitere Optimierung.

Das bringst du mit

Du hast bereits digitale Produkte entwickelt und weißt aus Erfahrung, dass eine gute Idee allein noch kein gutes Produkt ergibt.

  • Erfahrung im Produktmanagement: Du bringst mehrjährige Erfahrung als Product Owner oder Product Manager mit und hast digitale Produkte bereits eigenverantwortlich von der Konzeption bis zur Umsetzung begleitet.

  • Technisches Verständnis: Du kannst Anforderungen mit Entwickler*innen auf Augenhöhe besprechen, technische Abhängigkeiten nachvollziehen und daraus praktikable Lösungen ableiten. Erfahrung mit Low-Code-Plattformen ist ein Plus.

  • Sehr gute Figma-Kenntnisse: Du kannst selbstständig interaktive Prototypen entwickeln und hast ein fundiertes Verständnis von UX/UI und nutzerzentrierter Produktentwicklung.

  • Analytisches und strukturiertes Denken: Du erkennst frühzeitig, wenn Anforderungen nicht zusammenpassen, technische Voraussetzungen fehlen oder Prioritäten angepasst werden müssen.

  • Eigenständigkeit und Kommunikationsstärke: Du vertrittst deine fachliche Einschätzung klar und nachvollziehbar und behältst bei mehreren parallelen Themen den Überblick.

  • Agile Produktentwicklung: Du bist vertraut mit Scrum, Backlog-Management und Tools wie Asana. Du kennst außerdem Möglichkeiten, KI sinnvoll in digitalen Produkten und Prozessen einzusetzen.

  • Fundiertes Startup-Verständnis: Du verstehst den Lebenszyklus eines Startups – von der ersten Idee über die Gründung und den Markteintritt bis hin zu Wachstum und Skalierung. Du weißt, dass jede Phase unterschiedliche Herausforderungen mit sich bringt, und kannst dich schnell in die jeweiligen Bedürfnisse und Fragestellungen von Gründer*innen hineindenken. Eigene Gründungserfahrung ist ein Plus, aber keine Voraussetzung.

  • Verhandlungssichere Deutschkenntnisse und gute Englischkenntnisse

Das bieten wir dir

  • Ein Produkt mit Gestaltungsspielraum: Du bist früh in die Entwicklung eines neuen Plattformprojekts eingebunden und kannst Konzepte, Funktionen und Nutzererlebnisse aktiv mitgestalten.

  • Einfluss auf die Umsetzung: Deine fachliche Einschätzung ist ausdrücklich gefragt. Du arbeitest direkt mit Geschäftsführung, Projektleitung und Entwicklungsteam zusammen.

  • Einen Arbeitsplatz direkt in einer der schönsten Straßen der Hamburger Altstadt (Deichstraße).

  • Grandiose Kollege*innen mit einem wertschätzenden, hilfsbereiten Spirit und einem zugänglichen Management, das immer ein offenes Ohr für dich hat.

  • Eine intensive und strukturierte Einarbeitung, die dich optimal auf deinen Job bei uns vorbereitet.

  • Ein Deutschland-Ticket oder eine Urban-Sports-Mitgliedschaft.

  • Ein faires Gehalt zwischen 55.000 € und 65.000 € brutto jährlich bei einer Vollzeitstelle – je nach Erfahrung und Qualifikation. Bei Teilzeit wird das Gehalt anteilig entsprechend der vereinbarten Wochenstunden berechnet.

  • Teilzeit- und Homeoffice-Möglichkeiten.

  • Feedback-, Vertrauens- und Duz-Kultur.

  • Snacks und Getränke.

  • Teamevents.

Wir freuen uns auf deine Bewerbung mit einer kurzen Info zu deinem möglichen Starttermin und deiner zeitlichen Verfügbarkeit (Wochenstunden und Tage). Bei Fragen steht dir Vanessa Klein gerne zur Verfügung.

arbeitnow:senior-people-specialist-hr-op.description:
Kurzbeschreibung

SPREAD baut Engineering Intelligence für komplexe Produkte. Unsere AI-native Plattform gibt Automobilherstellern, Rüstungsunternehmen und Industriekonzernen eine vernetzte Sicht auf ihre Produktdaten. Volkswagen, BMW, Mercedes-Benz, Audi, Bosch und Rheinmetall arbeiten bereits damit. Hinter uns stehen HV Capital, DTCP, La Famiglia und Salesforce. Wir haben den SPARK AI Innovation Award gewonnen und stehen auf LinkedIns Liste der Top-Startups in DACH.
Die Rolle. Du baust die People-Programme von SPREAD auf: Performance, Karrierepfade, Compensation und Leadership Development. Von Februar bis November übernimmst du vertretungsweise unsere HR-Operations-Prozesse, die bereits gut eingespielt sind. Daneben bleibt genug Zeit, um parallel mit den ersten Strategiethemen zu starten. Ab November kommt unser Kollege aus HR Operations in Teilzeit zurück und übernimmt die Prozesse wieder. Ab dann liegt dein Fokus klar auf Strategie und Programmen. Du berichtest an Jasmina (People Lead). Unser People-Team ist bewusst schlank: Neben dir und Jasmina gehört eine Werkstudentin dazu, die das Office Management verantwortet und in HR hineinwächst, und ab November wieder unser Kollege aus HR Operations.
Wir setzen auf Talentdichte statt Headcount, und deine Programme sorgen dafür, dass Leistung sichtbar wird und sich lohnt. KI gehört bei uns überall dazu, im People-Team genauso. Sie setzt deine Gedanken schneller um, das Denken bleibt bei dir. Du bist mindestens drei Tage pro Woche bei uns im Office an der Köpenicker Straße, das ist gesetzt, denn HR passiert hier vor Ort. Wenn du Bock hast, People-Arbeit nicht nur zu verwalten, sondern aufzubauen, lies weiter.

Deine Verantwortung

  • Du gestaltest und fährst unseren Performance-Zyklus, von Evaluation-Frameworks über Kalibrierung bis zum Talent Board, damit Entscheidungen über Entwicklung und Gehalt nachvollziehbar sind.
  • Du entwickelst Career Frameworks und Leveling weiter, damit jede:r weiß, wo sie oder er steht und was als Nächstes kommt.
  • Du bereitest Compensation-Entscheidungen mit Daten vor, von Benchmarking über Gehaltsrunden bis zum Bonus.
  • Du bringst Leadership- und Manager-Formate an den Start, die unsere Führungskräfte spürbar besser machen.
  • Du steuerst interne Kommunikation und Pulse Surveys und leitest daraus Maßnahmen ab, die auch wirklich umgesetzt werden.
  • Du legst jedes Thema so vor, dass entschieden werden kann, mit Optionen und einer klaren Empfehlung.
  • Von Februar bis November verantwortest du vertretungsweise die HR-Administration von Vertrag bis Offboarding, betreibst Personio als Single Source of Truth und koordinierst die Payroll mit DATEV, pünktlich und ohne Gedöns.
  • Du automatisierst wiederkehrenden Papierkram selbst, damit Ops schlank läuft und dir Zeit für die Programme bleibt.
  • Du leitest unsere Werkstudentin an und entwickelst sie Richtung HR, damit sie dir Schritt für Schritt mehr Ops abnehmen kann.

Deine Erfahrung

Must-have

  • Ein abgeschlossenes Studium, idealerweise in (Wirtschafts-)Psychologie oder mit klarem HR-Schwerpunkt.
  • 3+ Jahre Erfahrung im HR Bereich, gerne im strategischen Bereich oder auch im operativen. Das heißt du kennst gängige best-practices, aktuelle Themen in der HR Welt und verschiedene Perspektiven auf wiederkehrende Herausforderungen in der Branche
  • Erfahrung in HR Operations, in denen du z.B. Verträge, On- und Offboarding oder die Payroll-Vorbereitung verantwortet hast.
  • Du hast ein HRIS eigenständig betreut und weißt, wie saubere Stammdaten aussehen.
  • Du hast mindestens ein People-Thema konzeptionell verantwortet, zum Beispiel Performance-Zyklen, Career Frameworks, Compensation oder Leadership-Entwicklung.
  • Arbeitsrecht kennst du so gut, dass du die meisten Fälle selbst löst und weißt, wann unsere Kanzlei ran muss.
  • Du baust einfache Automatisierungen selbst, nutzt KI-Tools wie Claude jeden Tag, weißt, was ein MCP ist, und prüfst Ergebnisse kritisch.
  • Du hältst Tagesgeschäft und ein, zwei Konzeptthemen parallel am Laufen, ohne dass etwas liegen bleibt.
  • Du denkst bei jeder Entscheidung mit, wie sie bei den Leuten ankommt, führst schwierige Gespräche ruhig und klar, und Vertrauliches bleibt bei dir.
  • Du sprichst fließend Deutsch und Englisch.

Strong plus

  • Du kennst Personio und DATEV aus der Praxis.
  • Du hast einen Master.
  • Du hast schon eine Werkstudentin, einen Werkstudenten oder Juniors angeleitet.
  • Du hast in einem schnell wachsenden Startup gearbeitet.
  • Du hast einen Führerschein.

Warum SPREAD?

Wir verkaufen KI für Engineering an große Automobil- und Industrieunternehmen, mit einem Produkt, das bei unseren Kunden produktiv läuft. Jedes Team bei uns arbeitet mit Claude-Agents, HR auch. Du baust die People-Seite eines Scale-ups auf, nicht die Verwaltung eines Konzerns, und arbeitest dabei direkt mit der People Lead und den Foundern. Dazu bekommst du ein wettbewerbsfähiges Gehalt, ein jährliches Lernbudget, ein Deutschlandticket, Urban Sports Club, 30 Urlaubstage plus einen bezahlten Volunteering-Tag und dreimal pro Woche Lunch im Office.
So stellen wir ein. Ein Erstgespräch, ein Fachgespräch und dann ein Auswahltag mit einer praktischen Challenge, einem Fit-Interview und gegebenenfalls einem Founder-Interview. Vom ersten Gespräch bis zum Angebot vergeht meist weniger als ein Monat. Du erfüllst nicht jeden Punkt? Bewirb dich trotzdem. Wir schauen uns jede Bewerbung genau an.

Dmytro İefymenko

arbeitnow:fullstack-engineer-prospect-da.description:
About You

You have a knack for solving intricate Software Development problems. You're driven by the idea of writing code that simplifies life for millions of users globally. You're committed to continuous learning and enjoy tackling new challenges. Pair programming, code reviews, and collaborative brainstorming with a team are activities you find fulfilling. You're eager to work alongside developers, prospective customers, account executives, product managers, data scientists, and data analysts. You're a disciplined professional who consistently delivers high-quality code that you take full ownership of, communicates technical solutions with clarity and empathy, and takes the initiative to streamline processes for your team and yourself.

About Us

Constructor is the next-generation platform for search and discovery in ecommerce, built on a unique GPT-based architecture made specifically for commerce. Constructor's AI-first solutions make it easier for shoppers to discover products they want to buy and for ecommerce teams to deliver highly personalized experiences, from search, to recommendations, to AI Shopping Agents and everything in between. Optimizing specifically for ecommerce metrics like revenue, conversion rate and profit, Constructor generates consistent $10M+ lifts for some of the biggest brands in ecommerce, such as Sephora, Petco, Under Armour, home24, Birkenstock and The Very Group. Constructor is a U.S. based company that has been in the market since 2019. It was founded by Eli Finkelshteyn and Dan McCormick who still lead the company today.

We’re a passionate team who love solving problems and want to make our customers’ and coworkers’ lives better. We value empathy, openness, curiosity, continuous improvement, and are excited by metrics that matter. We believe that empowering everyone in a company to do what they think is best can lead to great things.

About the Position

As a Software Engineer on the Prospect UI Solutions team, you will play a pivotal role in proving how Constructor will enhance the website discovery experiences for prospects. You’ll work closely with internal Engineering, Product and Sales stakeholders to seamlessly integrate prospective customer data with our services, supporting them to create an optimized and accurate product discovery demo.

In this role, you will:

  • Fuel our proprietary AI models: Write JavaScript code to collect data essential for training our AI.

  • Leverage Modern Tooling: Utilize AI as a tool to accelerate your fundamental capabilities and knowledge on how to solve problems with software; building solutions that you are proud to call your own

  • Seal the deal: Collaborate with Data Analysts and Account Executives to secure deals with prominent e-commerce brands.

  • Leverage your tech knowledge: Assist prospects in integrating their data and user interfaces with our services, focusing on ETL and front-end integrations.

  • Deliver excellence: Validate the data provided by prospects and ensure the quality of the results returned by our services.

  • Empower a sales force: Contribute to the development and scaling of demo infrastructure to enhance the demo capabilities of the Sales team.

  • Be a part of the answer: Assist Account Executives by addressing technical inquiries from prospects about our services.

  • Elevate the team: Provide support to your teammates through thoughtful code reviews and empathetic problem solving sessions.

  • Visualize brilliance: Develop dashboards and alerts using React, Redux, Node, Clickhouse and OpenSearch.

  • Innovate with purpose: Implement and test new features for our open-source JavaScript UI libraries and REST clients.

  • Collaborative contribution: Steer cross-team efforts to ensure our prospect's needs are at the forefront of our priorities, making you a key player in our strategic success.

  • Champion team culture: Actively foster our team’s sense of community by expanding our roster of Friday team-building games and promoting a culture of empathy, personal growth, and support for others.

This role is ideal for any Software Engineer passionate about search technology, customer-focused solutions, and collaborative development.

Requirements

  • A minimum of four years of professional experience or relevant academic experience

  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills

  • English on C1 level (CEFR) or higher

  • Being able to attend regular meetings with teammates between 1400 and 1800 UTC, with working hours ideally starting some time in the range of 0900 and 1200 UTC.

  • Strong foundation and experience with server-side and client-side programming languages

  • Enjoys interacting with customers and solving new problems daily

  • Able to pick up new technologies and design patterns quickly and loves learning them

  • Experience with building User Interfaces utilizing front-end frameworks like (but not limited to) React, Vue or Angular

  • Proven track record of building UIs with heavy consideration for friendly user experience

  • Experience with automated tests like (but not limited to) Cypress, Jest, or React Testing Library

  • Experience in JavaScript will be a strong asset for this role, but candidates with a proven Software Development background that demonstrate a willingness to quickly learn the language will also be considered

  • Nice to have - TypeScript, Next.js, Tailwind, Storybook, Python and web scraping experience

Benefits

  • 🏝️ Unlimited vacation time - we strongly encourage all of our employees take at least 3 weeks per year

  • 🌎 Fully remote team - choose where you live

  • 🛋️ Work from home stipend! We want you to have the resources you need to set up your home office

  • 💻 Apple laptops provided for new employees

  • 🧑‍🎓 Training and development budget for every employee, refreshed each year

  • 👪 Maternity & Paternity leave for qualified employees

  • 🧠 Work with smart people who will help you grow and make a meaningful impact

  • 🎉 Regular team offsites to connect and collaborate

Compensation

The base salary for this role starts at $80K+ USD for Mid-level and $90K+ USD for Senior. Your starting salary will depend on your experience, skills, and the level we align on during the interview process.

 

🎯 Experience level: We actively recruit Mid-level Engineers and above to support high productivity in our remote-first environment. We are not currently hiring for entry-level or Junior Engineer positions.

Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion at Constructor

At Constructor.io we are committed to cultivating a work environment that is diverse, equitable, and inclusive. As an equal opportunity employer, we welcome individuals of all backgrounds and provide equal opportunities to all applicants regardless of their education, diversity of opinion, race, color, religion, gender, gender expression, sexual orientation, national origin, genetics, disability, age, veteran status or affiliation in any other protected group.

Studies have shown that women and people of color may be less likely to apply for jobs unless they meet every one of the qualifications listed. Our primary interest is in finding the best candidate for the job. We encourage you to apply even if you don’t meet all of our listed qualifications.

How we handle your data. By submitting this application, you acknowledge that Constructor will collect and process the personal data you provide for the purpose of evaluating your candidacy for this role. If you are not selected, we will retain your data for a limited period as described in our Recruitment Privacy Notice. After that period your data will be deleted or anonymized.

arbeitnow:data-science-lead-hamburg-2514.description:
Data Science Lead

The adjoe Ads Data Science team owns the entire bidding algorithm that decides which ad you are most likely to enjoy from start to finish: conversion prediction, user quality estimation, and bid shading. Every bid adjoe placed in an ad auction is the output of ML models making 50 billion predictions daily, trained on data from our mobile SDKs that capture real user behavior at scale.

The team moves fast: new ideas tested offline, A/B tests launched in production within minutes. We rely on industry-proven state of the art technology, adapted to our needs and self-hosted where it matters: PyTorch and TensorFlow for modeling, Trino and Athena for querying a 350TB Iceberg data lake, Airflow and Ray for orchestrating our different training pipelines across multiple GPU clusters. Models are built on 600+ features and trained on 200 million data points, with the full ML lifecycle owned by the team from research and experimentation to deployment and real-time inference at sub-200ms latency.

Your Mission & Who We Are Looking For:

  • Hands-on People Leadership: You are a good listener and navigator, you inspire and empower your colleagues to florish. You will directly manage a team of Data Scientists and Data Analysts, owning 1-on-1s, performance reviews, and career growth. You are able to spot great modeling work, catch blockers like GPU limits or data quality issues, and brainstorm directly with the team rather than passing questions along.

  • Pragmatic Execution & Adaptive Process: You will build lightweight workflows for A/B testing, code reviews, incident management, and AI agent usage, introducing stricter structures only as our products mature. With a "hacker mindset," you prioritize shipping over bureaucracy, know when to balance experimentation with focus, and embed code hygiene into daily routines instead of one-off cleanup days.

  • Technical Fluency & Root-Cause Instinct: While not coding daily, you read Python, write SQL, use Git, and understand how technical systems work and what they cost under the hood. You use your analytical background to spot early warning signs in data, code, or team dynamics and trace them to their root cause.

  • Roadmap Co-Ownership & Business Alignment: You will partner with Staff Data Scientists to shape the roadmap while bridging business stakeholders and tech teams. You prioritize ideas by business impact, translate requirements into technical realities for the team, and align competing perspectives when multiple valid opinions exist.

  • Problem-First Ownership & Pace: You drive projects forward, refusing to accept "it doesn't work" as an answer and finding ways to make solutions viable. You push back when execution slows down, start with the problem before the solution, and know when to move fast versus when to double-check everything.

  • Plus: A formal background in mathematics and prior hands-on experience as a Data Science IC.

    What’s in It for You?

    At adjoe, you’re not here to just close JIRA tickets, you’re helping build the infrastructure behind one of the most impactful platforms in adtech. The systems you work on will reach hundreds of millions of users and power billions of decisions every day.

    • Go Big. Own projects with impact on 770M users and push adtech boundaries.

    • Move Fast. Ship solutions multiple times a day, learn from results, and keep momentum.

    • Be Direct. Solve problems openly and collaborate across teams.

    • Thrive Together. Grow with a diverse, global team of people from over 40 different countries that learn from each other.

    • Have Fun. Celebrate wins, enjoy daily victories, and bring your energy.

    We welcome applications from people who will contribute to the diversity of our company.

About Odys

At Odys, we’re mobilizing power, with Hybrid Power Systems developed for aerospace and in-demand everywhere. It’s the kind of mission diversity that demands a fresh way of thinking.

We began with an early bet on hybrid, when the mobility industry was focused on batteries. We designed, tested, and validated our first 1 MW high-speed generator in 12 months. And then we pushed further, developing systems with greater power density in less time. Today, our Hybrid Power Systems offer outputs ranging from 20 kW to 4 MW, with applications in the air or on the ground.

One of those applications is Laila, an unmanned drone designed for critical logistics and defense missions. With its 100 kW-class onboard Hybrid Power System, Laila can support medical cold-chain transport or serve as an aerial platform for counter-UAS measures.

The market interest has been overwhelming: Over 30 inbound requests from leading US and global manufacturers, and 14+ DoD contracts.

Our team comes from deep tech and aerospace, with backgrounds spanning drone and aircraft development, high-volume production, and electrified mobility.

We operate with urgency and ownership at every level. We validated high-speed generator technology faster than our peers, not because we skipped steps, but because we've been doing this long enough to know which ones matter most.

Creating the future of power, in the air and on the ground, is a challenge we’ve been training our entire lives for. If that sounds like you, this is the opportunity you’ve been waiting for.

 

About The Role

Odys Aviation is seeking a senior airworthiness lead for our UAS portfolio, starting with Laila, our hybrid-electric VTOL UAS for logistics and defense missions. The role sits with Odys Aviation GmbH in Munich, our European entity, and works daily with our engineering and test teams in the US.

The path is set: SORA SAIL III, then SAIL IV with an EASA DVR under SC Light-UAS, then DOA under Part 21 Subpart J and RTC or TC for larger products. EASA is our lead authority. The FAA is equally in scope, and our customers bring authorities from Europe, the Middle East, and APAC to the table.

This is a builder role. There is no legacy DOA to inherit and no large compliance department to delegate to. You set up design assurance in a way that fits a fast-moving hardware team, verify evidence yourself, and stay close to the aircraft through lab, ground, and flight testing.

You bridge two cultures: US engineering speed and European certification rigor. You know where the rules are still being written, and you help write them. Your credibility with authorities is an asset for the company, and your judgment on where effort pays off is an asset for the team.

Don't meet all desired requirements? Studies have shown that some people are less likely to apply to jobs unless they meet every single desired qualification. At Odys, we are dedicated to building an authentic workplace, so if you're excited about this role but your experience doesn't align perfectly with every desired qualification in the job description, we encourage you to apply anyway.

What You'll Do

  • Own SORA compliance strategy and evidence for SAIL III and SAIL IV, including the EASA DVR from application to closure

  • Obtain operational authorizations across jurisdictions from one evidence base

  • Drive design assurance across the group and perform compliance verification of engineering evidence reports

  • Build DOA readiness for higher SAIL, RTC, and TC

  • Set the regulatory frame for each test campaign and turn compliance needs into lab, ground, and flight test objectives that earn compliance credit

  • Ensure flight test safety reviews are timely and run with certification rigor; back up the Safety Lead

  • Represent Odys in EASA and FAA rulemaking, JARUS, EUROCAE, ASTM, SAE, RTCA, and GAMA

What We're Looking For

  • Degree in aerospace or a related engineering discipline

  • Substantial experience (typically 10+ years) in airworthiness or certification, including 5+ years on UAS or AAM, of 15+ years job experience

  • Expert command of FAA, EASA, and international aircraft certification frameworks

  • EASA: Regulations (EU) 2019/945 and 2019/947, SC Light-UAS, SC-VTOL, DVR process, Part 21 Subpart J

  • FAA: Part 107, Part 108, 21.17(b), powered-lift, MOSAIC

  • Strong command of JARUS SORA 2.0 and 2.5 at OSO and mitigation level, with a focus on Specific category authorizations at SAIL III or higher

  • Excellent compliance demonstration expertise, including flight test as a key means of compliance under JARUS SORA

  • Strong human factors experience on crewed or uncrewed aircraft

  • Track record in EASA and FAA rulemaking activities, and in leading roles in standards bodies

  • Established standing with authorities and with engineering leadership

  • Excellent English

Nice to Have

  • Experience working in export-controlled environments (e.g. EU Dual-Use Regulation, German AWG/AWV, U.S. EAR/ITAR) and with export compliance processes.

  • Hands-on lab, ground, or flight test experience; formal flight test training

  • Chief of the Office of Airworthiness or CVE experience in a Part 21 DOA

  • Hybrid-electric propulsion system experience

  • German language skills

Development Path

Natural candidate to grow into Chief of the Office of Airworthiness of our Part 21 Subpart J Design Organization, subject to program needs, demonstrated performance, and EASA acceptance.

arbeitnow:data-scientist-optimization-co.description:
Role

You’ll improve and extend the decision logic behind our battery fleet. Our optimization already runs our batteries every day; now we want to make it sharper, more robust and ready for new use cases. Our batteries sit behind the meter at industrial sites, so every decision has to balance customer savings, grid constraints and market value under uncertainty. Our data scientists and quantitative researchers work as one team and often across each other's topics.

 

What you will do

The role covers two closely linked areas. You can work in either one and switch between them as priorities and your interests evolve:

  • Fleet optimization: Plan how each battery runs over the coming hours and days, combining customer savings, grid fee rules and market value within each site's limits. Forecasts of load, PV and prices are generated and fed into the plan, which has to stay robust to their uncertainty. You also measure how much value we actually capture.

  • On-site control: Make the plan work in reality. Within our local control system, you design the logic that executes the schedule at each site, reacts to deviations and falls back safely when data or devices fail, while hard limits such as grid capacity, feed-in restrictions and state of charge always hold.

 

Topics you'll work on

You join work that is already running and take ownership of topics as priorities require. These are the areas where we want to add strength:

  • Improving and extending our optimization models for sequential decision-making on time series, across customer savings, grid fee rules and market value.

  • Making decisions more robust to forecast uncertainty (load, PV, prices).

  • Developing the on-site decision logic of our local control system: MPC, constraint handling and fallbacks.

  • Making sure hard constraints always hold in operation: grid connection limits, feed-in restrictions, state of charge.

  • Analyzing where we lose value compared to what was possible, and simulating new use cases before go-live.

  • Bringing models into production together with our engineers.

 

What we are looking for

  • Strong in optimization or control under uncertainty, e.g. LP/MILP, MPC, stochastic or robust optimization, state estimation or Kalman filtering.

  • Experience with, or at least exposure to, predictive modeling and machine learning, or a strong background in statistics.

  • Good Python skills and the ambition to write clean code that runs in production, not just in notebooks. You don't need to be a software engineer by training, but you care about code quality and use AI tools to move fast.

  • You are comfortable with messy real-world time-series data and team up with our data engineers to clean and prepare it for modeling.

  • You think in constraints and failure cases and make pragmatic decisions without perfect requirements.

  • You enjoy working closely in a small team, learning each other's topics and covering for each other.

  • Nice to have: battery storage, microgrids or energy management; using probabilistic forecasts in decision-making; German energy markets and regulation.

 

What it means to work at BEO

  • We are a small team taking on a hard problem, and we hold ourselves to a high bar. We value ownership, direct and honest communication, and getting better every day. If you like solving complex problems, you'll fit right in.

  • Our office is in central Munich. We offer plenty of flexibility but ask for an office-first commitment. People learn faster and get more done together.

  • You'll join us early in our journey. The foundations are in place, but it's still essentially day one, with plenty of opportunity to shape how we tackle one of the most significant challenges of our time.

About Us

Constructor is the next-generation platform for search and discovery in ecommerce, built to explicitly optimize for metrics like revenue, conversion rate, and profit. Our search engine is entirely invented in-house utilizing transformers and generative LLMs, and we use its core and personalization capabilities to power everything from search itself to recommendations to shopping agents. Engineering is by far our largest department, and we’ve built our proprietary engine to be the best on the market, having never lost an A/B test to a competitive technology. We’re passionate about maintaining this and work on the bleeding edge of AI to do so.

Out of necessity, our engine is built for extreme scale and powers over 1 billion queries every day across 150 languages and roughly 100 countries. It is used by some of the biggest ecommerce companies in the world like Sephora, Under Armour, and Petco.

We’re a passionate team who love solving problems and want to make our customers’ and coworkers’ lives better. We value empathy, openness, curiosity, continuous improvement, and are excited by metrics that matter. We believe that empowering everyone in a company to do what they do best can lead to great things.

Constructor is a U.S. based company that has been in the market since 2019. It was founded by Eli Finkelshteyn and Dan McCormick who still lead the company today.


The Team

The Core Team sits at the heart of Constructor, shaping Constructor’s in-house search engine, where user requests meet customer catalogs and Constructor’s learnings. We build and operate the foundational systems that power every request flowing through the platform, enabling fast, reliable, and intelligent interactions at massive scale.

Our systems handle billions of requests daily with exceptional uptime, and we take pride in delivering a highly scalable, resilient, and globally distributed platform. As part of the Core team, you will help design, build, and maintain the critical infrastructure and services that underpin the entire product, ensuring performance, stability, and reliability across the globe.


Requirements

You’ll thrive in this role if you:

  • Have a strong foundation in computer science, including algorithms, data structures, concurrency, and systems design.

  • Have experience building and scaling high-traffic, high-availability backend systems.

  • Have experience designing and operating backend infrastructure, including deployment automation, capacity planning, and observability.

  • Are comfortable working across different layers of the stack, from performance-critical code to production operations.

  • Enjoy learning new technologies and tools in a fast-moving, large-scale environment.

  • Collaborate effectively and contribute to a positive, ownership-driven team culture.

Our Tech Stack

  • Languages: Rust, C++, Python

  • Cloud Infrastructure: AWS

  • CI/CD: Jenkins, GitHub Actions

  • Monitoring & Observability: Prometheus, Grafana


Benefits

  • 🏝️ Unlimited vacation time - we strongly encourage all of our employees take at least 3 weeks per year

  • 🌎 Fully remote team - choose where you live

  • 🛋️ Work from home stipend! We want you to have the resources you need to set up your home office

  • 💻 Apple laptops provided for new employees

  • 🧑‍🎓 Training and development budget for every employee, refreshed each year

  • 👪 Maternity & Paternity leave for qualified employees

  • 🧠 Work with smart people who will help you grow and make a meaningful impact

  • 📈 Stock options - offered in addition to the base salary

  • 🎉 Regular team offsites to connect and collaborate

Compensation

The base salary for this role starts at $80K+ USD for Mid-level and $90K+ USD for Senior. Your starting salary will depend on your experience, skills, and the level we align on during the interview process.

 

🎯 Experience level: We actively recruit Mid-level Engineers and above to support high productivity in our remote-first environment. We are not currently hiring for entry-level or Junior Engineer positions.


Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion at Constructor

At Constructor.io we are committed to cultivating a work environment that is diverse, equitable, and inclusive. As an equal opportunity employer, we welcome individuals of all backgrounds and provide equal opportunities to all applicants regardless of their education, diversity of opinion, race, color, religion, gender, gender expression, sexual orientation, national origin, genetics, disability, age, veteran status or affiliation in any other protected group.

Studies have shown that women and people of color may be less likely to apply for jobs unless they meet every one of the qualifications listed. Our primary interest is in finding the best candidate for the job. We encourage you to apply even if you don’t meet all of our listed qualifications.

How we handle your data. By submitting this application, you acknowledge that Constructor will collect and process the personal data you provide for the purpose of evaluating your candidacy for this role. If you are not selected, we will retain your data for a limited period as described in our Recruitment Privacy Notice. After that period your data will be deleted or anonymized.

arbeitnow:customer-success-leader-enterp.description:
Why Harvey

At Harvey, we’re transforming how legal and professional services operate. By combining frontier agentic AI, an enterprise-grade platform, and deep domain expertise, we’re reshaping how critical knowledge work gets done for decades to come.

This is a rare chance to help build a generational company at a true inflection point. We have strong product-market fit and world-class investor support. We’re scaling fast and defining a new category in real time. The work is ambitious, the bar is high, and the opportunity for growth — personal, professional, and financial — is unmatched.

Our team moves fast, takes ownership, and is deeply committed to the mission — operating with intensity, staying close to our customers, and pushing each other for excellence. We live by three values: Decisiveness, Simplicity, and Job's Not Finished. We act quickly on clear judgment over perfect information, we believe simplicity is what scales, and we're never satisfied with where we are. If you want to do the best work of your career alongside people who share that drive, we'd love to build with you.

At Harvey, the future of professional services is being written today — and we’re just getting started.

Role Overview

As Customer Success Leader, you lead the team that is custodian of value for Harvey's Enterprise law-firm customers across Northern Europe. You own gross and net revenue retention across the segment, built on Harvey becoming embedded in how each firm's practice groups work and every firm moving along the AI maturity curve. You will be a visible executive presence with managing partners and firm leadership across a portfolio of prestigious, high-profile firms.

As a member of the broader Customer Success leadership team, you will set the strategy, playbooks and operating rhythm that let every CSM run their book as a portfolio and deliver a consistently high standard for every firm.

Through empathetic leadership and a high bar, you will hire and develop CSMs into trusted advisers to innovation leaders, practice group leaders and managing partners, so partners and associates see undeniable value and each firm builds a lasting AI advantage.

You will also partner across Harvey's go-to-market, product and legal engineering teams to shape how we serve law firms end to end.

What You'll Do

  • Build and lead a high-performing team: hire, coach and develop Enterprise Law Firm CSMs across Northern Europe, promoting a culture of accountability, execution, growth and relentless improvement.

  • Own retention, expansion and renewal readiness: run the segment as a portfolio — knowing, with evidence, whether each firm needs protecting or growing — surface risk early, build expansion plans with Sales where there is room to grow, ensure every firm is multi-threaded, and forecast accurately against gross and net revenue retention targets.

  • Prove value: coach your team to align each firm on measurable outcomes — capacity, realisation, matter economics, client impact — and capture the value stories and ROI evidence that underpin renewal and growth.

  • Lead at partner level: grow CSMs into trusted advisers who cultivate champions and partner sponsors, and engage directly with managing partners, senior partners and innovation leaders at the segment's key firms.

  • Set the standard for the firm's journey: define and scale the playbooks — mutual success plans tied to each firm's objectives, kickoffs, implementation reviews, QBRs and executive business reviews — that take every firm from pilot to daily use, practice group by practice group.

  • Orchestrate cross-functionally: partner with Sales, Legal Engineering, Innovation Partners, the Transformation Office and Product leaders so each firm gets the right expertise at the right moment.

  • Run the product feedback flywheel: turn the voice of law-firm customers into prioritised input for Product and Engineering, and into improvements in how we deliver.


What You Have

Ideal candidates for the Customer Success Leader, Enterprise Law Firms role at Harvey can demonstrate comfort and experience with the following:

  • A proven background leading high-performing Customer Success or account management teams in late-stage or post-IPO enterprise SaaS, serving strategic or lighthouse accounts with substantial six-figure annual spend — ideally law firms or other professional services firms.

  • A track record of owning and delivering a team-level revenue, retention or net-revenue-retention number, with accurate forecasting.

  • Building teams through hiring, coaching and developing talent, with a leadership style grounded in empathy and a high bar.

  • Designing and scaling playbooks that take enterprise customers from initial adoption to embedded, organisation-wide use, with measurable outcomes grounded in concrete use cases.

  • Building multi-threaded relationships at senior level and influencing partners and stakeholders who did not buy the product.

  • Portfolio planning and revenue-based prioritisation across a regional book, including early identification and mitigation of risk.

  • Quantifying and communicating business value and ROI to senior legal stakeholders.

  • An AI-native way of working: you use AI and sophisticated tooling daily, can show how it has changed your own and your team's output, and have a point of view on how AI changes legal practice.

  • Communicating and influencing at every level, internally and externally, including running in-person meetings with managing partners and firm leadership.

  • Law-firm experience is a strong plus: an understanding of how partnerships make decisions, how practice groups differ and what partners, associates and innovation teams each care about, ideally in the Northern European legal market.

  • Adapting seamlessly in the face of high-speed change and growth, with a strong point of view and proactive self-management.

You’ll own our presence on LinkedIn, X, and YouTube with video at the center: clipping talks, podcasts, launches, and live moments into content that travels, building formats people come back for, and working with the creators developers already trust. You’ll be accountable for growing audience and engagement across a global community.

You’ll sit on the Story & Communications team, reporting to the Head of Story & Communications, and work closely with developer relations, product marketing, demand generation, events, and our brand and design team. This is a hands-on role: you’ll make the work, not only schedule it.

  • Put video at the center of how ClickHouse shows up: clip talks, podcasts, livestreams, launches, and executive moments into short-form and vertical content, and build recurring, social-first series that earn a following

  • Build a brand developers find interesting at the intersection of infrastructure, technology, and culture, pairing technical depth with humor, opinion, and craft

  • Work with the creators and technical voices developers already follow, through collaborations, co-created content, guest appearances, and amplification, in tandem with developer relations and the wider marketing team

  • Turn launches, announcements, customer stories, and research into social moments, and bring live coverage from Open House and industry events, working with regional teams so local moments reach a global audience

  • Grow the voices around the brand: partner with communications on executive presence on LinkedIn and X, and give employees and developer advocates what they need to share their work

  • Own the numbers for organic social, including audience growth, engagement, video performance, and share of the developer conversation, and report on what’s working and why

  • Track what developers say about ClickHouse and the category and feed it back to product marketing, developer relations, and campaign teams, while using AI tooling and a lean production workflow to ship content quickly and partnering with demand generation so the best organic work gets paid reach

What You Bring Along

  • A record of growing audience and engagement at scale for a brand with a global following, and the numbers to show it

  • Real fluency with video: you can shoot, edit, and clip yourself, you know what makes short-form and vertical content work on each platform, and you can find the best ninety seconds in an hour-long talk

  • Experience running influencer or creator programs: finding the right voices, structuring partnerships, and making the collaboration feel native to the creator’s audience

  • Experience with a technical or B2B audience, and the ability to turn technical substance into something people want to share

  • Preferred: experience in SaaS, developer tools, or infrastructure

  • Taste and a point of view on internet culture: you know where developers spend time online, what they find funny, and what makes them tune a brand out

  • Sharp short-form writing: the post, the hook, the caption, the thread

  • A builder’s approach: you test quickly, read the data honestly, scale what works, and drop what doesn’t

  • Comfort owning a channel end to end while working across many teams, with low ego and high standards

Perks

As part of a rapidly scaling start-up, you will be instrumental in shaping our culture.

We are seeking a Senior Manager, UK Security to establish and lead the UK industrial security capability required to pursue and deliver sensitive Ministry of Defence, allied-government, and prime-contractor programmes.

This hands-on leader will serve as Shield AI's senior UK security adviser and, subject to government approval and contractual need, perform the appropriate Facility Security Controller and Personnel Security Controller responsibilities.   • Lead readiness for Facility Security Clearance (FSC) and Industry Personnel Security Assurance (IPSA), including gap assessments, secure-site preparations, evidence, corrective actions, and continuing assurance.

  • Coordinate with Cybersecurity and IT on secure systems, remote-working controls, government assurance, incident response, and remediation.

  • Work with product security, engineering, Cybersecurity and programme teams to identify UK customer security requirements early, support Secure by Design activities, and ensure product security risks, decisions and assurance evidence are tracked through the lifecycle.

  • Manage UK security incidents, aftercare reporting, foreign ownership or influence concerns, insider and supply-chain risks, and required government notifications.

  • Build metrics, budgets, vendors, and the UK security team as the business grows; support occasional out-of-hours response and UK or international travel.

Preferred Qualifications

arbeitnow:biomedical-scientist-birmingha.description:
Mission

Neko Health is a health technology company that opened its first clinic in Stockholm in 2018, founded by Daniel Ek and Hjalmar Nilsonne.

In one hour, our scan combines radiation-free imaging, heart and circulation measurements, and same-visit blood results with time to talk it through with a clinician, so people can act on what matters before symptoms appear. We design and build our own hardware, software and clinical protocols, and more than 100,000 members have already had a scan, with 75% booking and prepaying their next one before they leave.

As a team, we chase 10X, not 10%, and we’re looking for people who think the same way to help us scale what we’ve started in Sweden, the UK, and now the US. Join the clinicians, engineers and business builders making prevention a routine part of care.

Role Purpose

This is not a traditional laboratory role. We're looking for a Biomedical Scientist who is comfortable working differently, embraces innovation, and takes pride in delivering accurate results at exceptional pace.

Neko Health members come through our clinics for whole-body preventive health screenings, and our laboratories sit at the centre of the patient journey. They are busy, modern spaces, and the service continues to develop as we scale.

This is a hands-on, autonomous role, based on site in one of our central London laboratories. As a Biomedical Scientist, you will operate our Abbott Alinity and Sysmex XN-550 analysers and support the quality systems that allow us to return results within 30 minutes of sample receipt.

If you're a BMS looking to further develop your career in an innovation-led environment, we would love to hear from you.

 

What You'll Deliver in the First 6 - 12 Months

  • Initialise the analysers each day and ready them for sample processing.

  • Perform testing on our Abbott Alinity (biochemistry and immunoassay) and Sysmex XN-550 (haematology) analysers, validating patient results and escalating clinically anomalous or unexpected findings.

  • Carry out daily calibration, internal quality control, and routine maintenance of analysers, troubleshooting and escalating technical issues promptly.

  • Work within our ISO 15189-aligned, UKAS-facing quality management system: author SOP updates, monitor EQA performance, support audits, and investigate non-conformances.

  • Contribute to service improvement work, including analyser verification, reagent evaluation, and software testing.

  • Maintain accurate, auditable records and support performance monitoring across turnaround times, KPIs, and consumables usage.

  • Provide technical guidance to clinical colleagues and support training across the lab team.

 

Minimum Requirements

  • HCPC registration as a Biomedical Scientist, with evidence of ongoing CPD.

  • Minimum one year of post-registration experience in clinical chemistry and immunoassay, including IQC and EQA practice.

  • Demonstrable experience operating an integrated clinical chemistry and immunoassay analyser.

  • Experience working accurately and efficiently under time pressure, suited to a low-volume, fast-turnaround service model.

 

Preferred

  • Post-registration experience in haematology.

  • Hands-on experience operating Sysmex XN-series haematology analysers.

  • Hands-on experience operating Abbott Alinity ci-series.

arbeitnow:area-medical-lead-north-midlan.description:
Mission

Neko Health is a health technology company that opened its first clinic in Stockholm in 2018, founded by Daniel Ek and Hjalmar Nilsonne.

In one hour, our scan combines radiation-free imaging, heart and circulation measurements, and same-visit blood results with time to talk it through with a clinician, so people can act on what matters before symptoms appear. We design and build our own hardware, software and clinical protocols, and more than 100,000 members have already had a scan, with 75% booking and prepaying their next one before they leave.

As a team, we chase 10X, not 10%, and we’re looking for people who think the same way to help us scale what we’ve started in Sweden, the UK, and now the US. Join the clinicians, engineers and business builders making prevention a routine part of care.

Role Purpose

You own the clinical bar across the Neko clinics in the North and Midlands (currently Birmingham and Manchester).

That means every consultation in your area meets the same threshold of safety, quality, and member experience across your region. It means the clinical teams working with you are developing, not just performing. It means clinical issues are being seen and addressed before they show up in audits or member complaints. And it means the quality metrics for your region are known, owned and moving in the right direction. And it means clinical judgment shows up at the table when operational decisions are being made.

You'll partner closely with the UK Medical Director, who holds final clinical authority for the UK market, and operate in true dyad partnership with the Area Clinic Manager for your region who owns the operational side. The clinical health of the region is yours.

What You'll Deliver in the First 6–12 Months

  • Hold the clinical standard across every site in your area

  • Manage and develop the clinicians in your region: performance conversations, development plans, coaching, and the honest feedback that turns good clinicians into great ones.

  • Ensure lead clinicians in your market(s) are performing excellently and that the clinical teams have the appropriate clinical escalation pathways in place.

  • Support clinical hiring for your area against defined criteria, and partner with the Training and Education team to close training gaps as they emerge.

  • Own the review and closure of clinical incidents and near-misses in your area, making sure learnings are actually applied, not just documented.

  • Own the quality metrics for your region: accountable for performance against Neko's medical quality goals at area level, including scan quality (perfect scan score), member follow-up quality and timeliness (perfect follow-up score and follow-up SLAs), clinical safety (Northstar Clinical Safety score) and clinician summary quality and timeliness. Review the data with your Area Clinic Manager each week and month, trace variation to root cause by site and clinician, set improvement actions, and report progress and risks to the UK Medical Director.

  • Operate in true dyad partnership with the Area Clinic Manager: co-owning quality, member experience, and business goals, attending and contributing to Weekly and Monthly Business Reviews, and bringing clinical input into operational decisions before they're made.

  • Round your sites regularly to observe, support, and listen, surfacing what's working so it can spread, and what isn't so it can be addressed.

  • Build and maintain trusted relationships with the GPs, NHS trusts and private specialist clinicians who receive Neko referrals, monitoring referral quality and addressing breakdowns quickly.

  • Know the UK regulatory landscape: CQC registration and inspection standards, GMC/NMC professional standards and revalidation, NHS and GP referral pathways and obligations, and UK-specific clinical rules, and flag emerging risks before they become problems.

  • Lead or participate in clinical pilots as required - defining success, capturing learnings, and documenting outcomes so the rest of the company can learn from your region.

What We're Hiring For

  • Holds the Bar at Scale. You're the kind of clinical leader who can make sure every consultation feels the same regardless of site or clinician, not by micromanaging, but by setting a clear standard, coaching to it, and noticing when it drifts. You're rigorous without being rigid.

  • Develops the Clinicians You Lead. You take clinician development seriously. You give honest feedback even when it's uncomfortable. You spot what someone needs before they ask. You know the difference between a clinician who needs coaching and one who needs to leave, and you don't avoid either conversation.

  • The Dyad That Actually Works. You bring clinical judgment into operational decisions before they're made and you stay constructive when clinical standards and operational targets pull in different directions. When you escalate, it's because something genuinely needs leadership attention, not because you've stopped trying to resolve it locally.

  • Reads the Pattern, Not Just the Report. You don't just review the data. You see what it's telling you. You round your sites and notice things that don't show up in dashboards. When you spot a pattern you trace it to the root cause and you make sure the right people hear about it.

  • Trusted Outside the Walls. The referral network, the regulators, the specialist clinicians who receive Neko members: these relationships sit with you. You represent Neko credibly because you're a credible clinician yourself. People in the local medical community know your name, and when you flag something, they take it seriously.

Minimum Requirements

  • Full GMC registration with a license to practice, in good standing and with a current revalidation, and right to work in the UK.

  • On the GMC GP Register with qualification (CCT or equivalent) in General Practice.

  • 4+ years of medical leadership experience in the UK health system (NHS and/or private sector), including direct management of clinicians.

  • Demonstrated experience holding clinical standards across multiple sites or a large clinical team.

Preferred

  • Experience in preventive care, tech enabled healthcare or longitudinal care models.

  • Experience operating in a clinical-operational dyad structure.

  • Experience leading clinical pilots or scaling new clinical workflows across multiple sites.

About Mistral

Mistral provides full-stack AI solutions: from frontier models to developer tools, applications, and compute. We partner with enterprises tackling the hardest problems across high-stakes industries like finance, manufacturing, defense, healthcare, and the public sector, co-creating customized AI systems that they can run on their terms.

We are a dynamic, collaborative team passionate about AI and its potential to transform society. Our diverse workforce thrives in competitive environments and is committed to driving innovation. Our teams are distributed between Europe, North America, Asia and the Middle East. We are creative, low-ego and team-spirited.

About the role

The Inference team builds and runs the systems that serve Mistral's models to the world.

We own the path from a trained model to a response on someone's screen. That includes the APIs and gateway that requests come through, routing and scheduling across our GPU fleet, and the capacity, deployment and operations work that keeps it all running.

Our work serves two groups. Customers need fast, reliable and cost-efficient inference as usage keeps growing. Our researchers rely on the same systems for evaluation, data generation and reinforcement learning, so what we build feeds directly into the next generation of models.

 

What You Will Do

As an Engineer on Inference, you'll build and run the services that sit between our users and our models. The work is close to the product and to the hardware, and the improvements you make show up quickly in latency, reliability, cost and how fast we can ship new models.

Experience with LLM inference is a plus, but it isn't a requirement. We're just as interested in strong Systems Engineers from other backgrounds who are keen to go deep on serving.

A few of the problems our teams work on:

  • Designing and evolving our inference APIs, so model capabilities like tool calling, structured outputs and new modalities are available to developers on launch day.

  • The backend services and gateway every request passes through, from authentication, streaming and rate limiting to usage metering, observability and end-to-end reliability.

  • Routing, load balancing and autoscaling across our clusters, so we absorb traffic spikes without wasting GPUs.

  • Faster, safer rollouts of new models and serving releases.

What We're Looking For

  • Have several years of experience shipping and running backend or distributed systems that serve real production traffic.

  • Write high-quality production code, and are comfortable using AI coding tools without compromising on it.

  • Care about performance and reliability, and enjoy making systems faster, cheaper and more robust.

  • Have led the design of significant systems, making the right trade-offs and seeing them through to production.

About DataCamp

DataCamp's mission is to empower everyone with the data and AI skills essential for 21st-century success. By providing practical, engaging learning experiences, DataCamp equips learners and organizations of all sizes to harness the power of data and AI. As a trusted partner to over 17 million learners and 6,000+ companies, including 80% of the Fortune 1000, DataCamp is leading the charge in addressing the critical data and AI skills shortage.

About the role

Research has consistently shown that one-on-one tutoring dramatically outperforms traditional classroom instruction—a finding known as Bloom's 2 Sigma Problem. Despite decades of awareness, no solution has successfully delivered personalized tutoring at scale. Until now.

We are building an AI tutoring system designed to emulate and eventually surpass the best human tutors. You will work on the core AI system that delivers real-time, adaptive learning experiences to learners. If you're excited about building the future of human learning, this role is for you. This role can be done remotely from anyone of the following; United Kingdom, Belgium, Portugal OR UAE

About you

At DataCamp, we seek individuals who embody our core values of data-driven decision-making, action, transparency, ownership, and customer focus. You thrive in a fast-paced, high-performing environment and are driven by a passion for making a meaningful impact. You're adaptable, embracing change and ambiguity with enthusiasm. Your initiative and entrepreneurial spirit push you beyond just meeting targets—you aim to understand the "why" behind our goals and take ownership to drive the business forward. You're a collaborative team player who values transparency and always seeks to improve and innovate. If this sounds like you, we encourage you to apply!

Responsibilities

  • Build and evolve the core AI tutoring system, including prompt architectures, agentic workflows, and real-time adaptive behaviors.
  • Run rigorous experimentation and evaluation, developing custom metrics and frameworks to measure learning effectiveness and improve model reliability.
  • Design and implement scalable, maintainable software, integrating AI capabilities with platform systems, content pipelines, and user experience components.
  • Collaborate cross-functionally with educators, content creators, and product teams to translate pedagogical goals into technical solutions.
  • Prototype and productionize novel model interactions, leveraging emerging research and capabilities to advance the tutor's intelligence.
  • Ensure quality, safety, and observability through monitoring, testing, guardrails, and iterative refinement of model behavior.
  • Share knowledge and elevate teammates, contributing to a culture of clarity, simplicity, and continuous learning.

arbeitnow:commercial-customer-success-ma.title: Commercial Customer Success Manager
arbeitnow:commercial-customer-success-ma.description:
A little about us

incident.io is the AI software reliability platform trusted by engineering teams at Notion, Linear, Ramp and 2,000+ companies who can't afford downtime.

The stakes are real, the talent is insane, and somehow it's a genuinely lovely place to work. We all pull our weight, go the extra mile, and put in the bit of magic most companies don't have time for, all while having fun and never taking ourselves too seriously.

We've raised $100+ million from Index Ventures, Insight Partners, and Point Nine, and we're growing fast. There's never been a better time to join.

The role in one line

Customers trust us when things go wrong. We're the software reliability platform built to investigate, respond to and prevent incidents. As a Commercial CSM, you're the partner to our mid-market engineering teams - getting them onboarded, embedded and expanding their usage, and maturing their incident management and reliability as they grow.

What that looks like day to day

Our Customer Success organisation is at the heart of incident.io. We're the team closest to our customers' hardest problems, and we're trusted to solve them. We believe in a customer-led product approach, working hand in hand with Product to uncover and address what each customer really needs. Our goal goes beyond satisfaction: we want to delight customers at every stage of their journey, and build long-term relationships grounded in trust, shared success and mutual growth.

You'll look after 70–80 Commercial customers: growth-oriented tech companies, mostly under 1,000 people, between $30k and $150k ARR each. Industry leaders like Vanta, Monday.com and Loom sit in this segment. Some are steady, some are scaling fast, and much of the job is knowing which is which, and what each one needs from you.

Most of your time goes to mid-market customers on our top-tier plan, where you're their dedicated CSM leading onboarding and adoption. You'll blend 1:1 time with scalable programmes to get teams to value quickly: best-practice sessions, end-user training, partnership and roadmap reviews. You'll also cover a subset of smaller customers in a low-touch capacity, leaning on usage data to spot risk and opportunity early.

Day to day, this is a high ownership role. You'll help customers navigate the product, unpick problems when they hit them, and keep everyone pointed at the outcomes their team actually cares about. You are responsible for proactively identifying expansion and upsell opportunities, and partnering with Sales and Expansion Account Managers to grow revenue within your accounts. Internally, you're the voice of the Commercial customer with Product, Engineering, Sales, Marketing and Support.

There's still a lot to build and a ton of opportunity for you to shape this segment. The Commercial motion works, but scaling and automating the customer journey is live work we're ramping up now - refining playbooks, automating the repeatable stuff, building the tooling and content that makes a portfolio this size easier to serve. We're AI-forward in how we approach it, so you'd be shaping this rather than inheriting it.

Who you are

  • You've carried a book of 40 to 100+ accounts and worked out how to be present across all of them without going quiet on half.

  • You've sold to, or supported, technical people, whether that's engineering teams, on-call rotations or developer tools. You can hold your own in a technical conversation without needing to escalate every one of them.

  • You've got commercial instincts. You spot the account that's about to double, you know what a growth signal looks like, and you know how to steer a renewal to a good outcome.

  • You know what scaled CS looks like when it's done well. Playbooks, one-to-many programs, AI-assisted workflows. You don't need to have built them from scratch, but you've worked around them enough to have opinions on what you'd do differently.

  • Half-built process doesn't rattle you. You'd rather fix the documentation than complain about it.

  • You actually like being in a room with customers, and you'll get on a plane for the right one.

Supporting you

We work hard and we think life outside work matters just as much. Our benefits pack is built to support both.

  • Private medical insurance. Seriously good cover — we want you and the people you love to be looked after.

  • Competitive annual leave. Showing up at your best requires switching off, and we make sure you have time to do that.

  • First Friday of every month off. Yes, seriously.

  • Enhanced pension. We put real money in, because future-you deserves better than an afterthought.

  • Meaningful equity. We're rapidly scaling, and everyone who helps shape the outcome should share in it.

  • Unlimited AI spend. For everyone, not just engineers. We're all-in on AI across the company, and we expect you to be too.

  • Generous parental leave. The early days with a new baby matter more than anything we're doing here, and we want you to be present for them.

  • Two budgets that have your back. £1000 to invest in your setup, £500 a year to invest in yourself.

Compensation: £85K – £118K • Offers Equity

  • London • £85K – £118K • Offers Equity

We’re Checkout.com. You might not know our name, but companies like eBay, Spotify, Klarna, Uber, and Sony do, because we’re behind many of the digital experiences you use every day.


We are where the world checks out, enabling over 10 billion transactions yearly for more than one billion global shoppers.

Whether you want to book a holiday, order food, renew a subscription, or check out online, there’s a good chance our tech powers the payments behind the scenes. Our platform helps the most ambitious businesses deliver effortless digital experiences, at scale.

If you want to do career-defining work, you’ve come to the right place. We move fast, think globally, and believe great teams are built by hiring exceptional people with conviction, curiosity, and the desire to make an impact.

With 20 offices across six continents and London as our HQ, we’re shaping the future of fintech – and we’re just getting started.

Checkout.com's Regional Events and Field Marketing Team support the end-to-end management and execution of hosted and sponsored events to drive business growth by partnering closely for our UK and Europe commercial teams. You will collaborate with expert regional marketers to develop and implement a comprehensive account-based marketing strategy, encompassing events, experiential marketing activities, and global initiatives. Your attention to detail, planning skills, and data-driven mindset ensure events align seamlessly with strategic goals.

How You’ll Make An Impact

As an Events Specialist, you'll support the execution of our Regional and Global events. You will work to build strong relationships with commercial teams and collaborate cross-functionally. Your responsibilities will span the entire event lifecycle, including:

  • Assist in developing and executing a regional event strategy, including the management of regional events, experiential marketing activities, and participation in major global initiatives, ensuring high-quality execution and alignment with company goals.

  • Support end-to-end event planning, including vetting, sourcing, budget management, and on-site execution, while coordinating with cross-functional teams for seamless event experiences.

  • Contribute to creating audience acquisition plans grounded in data-driven insights to drive pipeline generation. Leverage your customer-centric proficiency to help build audience targeting based on inputs (e.g., TAM, ICP, Personas).

  • Assist in managing key performance indicators (KPIs), reporting, data analysis, and providing comprehensive program performance summaries with actionable recommendations. Work with the team to identify new ways of optimising activity against KPIs.

  • Help with the meticulous planning and management of events, optimising processes for scalability and efficiency, and contribute to documentation of processes.

  • Use your excellent communication skills to convey complex thoughts and manage multiple external parties effectively.

  • Demonstrate strong project management skills, helping to deliver programs and activities within the team with the guidance of senior members.

What We’re Looking For

  • Proven experience in a similar role (3+ years), preferably in payments, fintech, or related sectors, or within an event agency.

  • In this hands-on and high-impact role, you\'re a self-starter, passionate about data, and proactive in pursuing new ideas.

  • Excellent organisational and project management skills, with the ability to juggle multiple projects effectively.

  • Ability to establish relationships with stakeholders of all levels to drive excellent collaboration.

  • Exceptional writing, communication, and presentation skills with good attention to detail.

  • Operational proficiency in event management software, marketing automation, and CRM systems (e.g., Salesforce, Pardot, Zoom, or other).

  • Willingness and ability to travel 20%-40% of the time for event management.

Additional Information

Bring all of you to work

Salience Labs is building an industry-defining approach to optical circuit switching for AI infrastructure, engineered for real latency reduction and cost savings. The Role

As Finance Director at Salience Labs, you will own financial control, compliance and reporting across our UK, German and US entities, supporting our business strategy in a fast-paced, high-tech scale-up. Reporting to the CFO and working closely with cross-functional teams, you will lead the finance function and stay hands-on, equally comfortable running a close and building the scalable processes that improve it.

Financial control and reporting

  • Run the monthly consolidation across three entities: review trial balances, translate currencies, reconcile intercompany accounts and post eliminations.

  • Prepare group management accounts, Board materials and project-based reporting (actuals and cash use against budget), explaining the movements that matter to leadership.

  • Lead annual budgeting and quarterly reforecasting across all entities, tracking actuals against plan and highlighting key variances.

  • Develop and implement internal control policies and procedures.

Statutory, tax and compliance

  • Prepare UK GAAP statutory accounts and VAT returns, work with advisers on corporation tax, manage HMRC and Companies House deadlines, and coordinate the year-end audit.

  • Work with our German tax adviser (Steuerberater) on local VAT and tax filings, and reconcile the statutory books to group reporting.

  • Ensure US tax and statutory compliance with external advisers.

Payroll, cash and operations

  • Prepare and review payroll across entities, post payroll journals, and reconcile payroll liability, tax and benefit control accounts.

  • Manage cash flow and oversee day-to-day finance operations for the US and German entities, including cash balances, supplier payments and expenses.

  • Support vendor negotiations and maintain key financial relationships.

Inventory, costing and assets

  • Own month-end inventory reconciliations and cost of sales tracking. Work with operations and engineering to verify quantities and values for raw materials, WIP and finished goods (including stock held at third-party sites), and investigate manufacturing variances.

  • Maintain and reconcile fixed asset, depreciation and prepayment schedules across entities.

Grants, R&D and strategic projects

  • Monitor and report on grant, R&D and contract expenditure, including preparing and submitting grant reimbursement claims.

  • Contribute to strategic projects, including share option scheme management.

Systems and process improvement

  • Implement and optimise our finance systems, from defining requirements and testing workflows to supporting users through the first close after launch.

What we're looking for

  • ACA, ACCA, CIMA or equivalent qualification, with a minimum of 10 years' post-qualification experience, including 5+ years in start-up or fast-growth environments.

  • Proven experience in financial controllership, personally preparing multi-currency group consolidations and UK statutory accounts, handling VAT returns and coordinating corporation tax filings, with UK payroll compliance and IFRS and/or GAAP knowledge.

  • Experience taking a finance system (accounting, expense or payroll) through implementation and its first close, including balance validation and workflow testing.

  • Experience managing inventory valuation, WIP or product costing in a hardware or manufacturing business.

  • Strong attention to detail, with clean reconciliations, accurate intercompany balances and reliable inventory figures.

  • A proactive mindset, anticipating process gaps and upcoming tax or audit deadlines early.

  • Practical problem-solving: digging into the root cause of variances across manufacturing costs and cross-border accounting rather than simply flagging them.
